title.zh: 卷三百四十四 列傳第一百〇三 孫覺 李常 孔文仲 李周 鮮于侁 顧臨 李之純 王覿 馬默
title.en: Volume 344 Biographies 103: Sun Jue, Li Chang, Kong Wenzhong, Li Zhou, Xian Yushen, Gu Lin, Li Zhichun, Wang Di, Ma Mo
title.raw: 卷三百四十四 列傳第一百〇三 孫覺 李常 孔文仲 李周 鮮于侁 顧臨 李之純 王覿 馬默 Volume 344 Biographies 103: Sun Jue, Li Chang, Kong Wenzhong, Li Zhou, Xian Yushen, Gu Lin, Li Zhichun, Wang Di, Ma Mo

sentences.zh: 神宗將大革積弊，覺言：「弊政固不可不革，革而當，其悔乃亡。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong was about to undertake great reform of accumulated abuses. Jue said: "Abusive policies indeed cannot go unreformed; when reform is done rightly, regret then ceases."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong was preparing to sweep away long-standing abuses, Sun Jue said, "Corrupt practices certainly must be reformed—but if the reforms are sound, regret will never come."

sentences.zh: 神宗稱其知理。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong praised him for understanding principle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him for grasping the point.

sentences.zh: 嘗從容語及知人之難，覺曰：「堯以知人為難，終享其易。

translations.literal: Once, speaking at ease about the difficulty of knowing men, Jue said: "Yao took knowing men to be difficult, yet in the end enjoyed its ease.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion, speaking casually about how hard it is to know people, Jue said, "Yao found knowing men difficult, yet in the end he enjoyed the ease that came of it.

sentences.zh: 蓋知人之要，在於知言。

translations.literal: For the essential point of knowing men lies in knowing their words.
translations.idiomatic: The key to knowing men lies in knowing what they say.

sentences.zh: 人主用臣之道，任賢使能而已。

translations.literal: The way a ruler employs ministers is simply to entrust the worthy and use the capable.
translations.idiomatic: A sovereign's way of using ministers is simply to entrust the worthy and employ the capable.

sentences.zh: 賢能之分既殊，任使之方亦異。

translations.literal: Since the categories of worthiness and capability differ, the methods of entrustment and employment also differ.
translations.idiomatic: Worthiness and capability are not the same thing, and the way you assign roles must differ accordingly.

sentences.zh: 至於所知有限量，所能有彼此，是功用之士也，可以處外而不可以處內，可以責之事而不可責之言。

translations.literal: As for those whose knowledge has limits and whose capabilities have their respective spheres—these are men of functional utility; they may be placed in external affairs but not in internal ones, and may be charged with deeds but not with words.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose knowledge is bounded and whose talents suit only certain tasks are men of practical utility: they may serve in outward affairs but not at the inner court, and you may hold them accountable for deeds but not for counsel.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲興太平之治，而所擢數十人者，多有口才，而無實行。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to raise the governance of Great Peace, yet of the several dozen men you have promoted, many have eloquence of speech but no substantive conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty wishes to bring about an age of great peace, yet among the several dozen men you have advanced, many are glib speakers with no real achievement to their credit.

sentences.zh: 臣恐日浸月長，彙征牆進，充滿朝廷之上，則賢人日遠，其為患禍，尚可以一二言之哉？

translations.literal: I fear that day by day and month by month they will gather and advance like ants scaling a wall, filling the court above—then the worthy will daily grow more distant. The harm and calamity this would bring—can it even be stated in one or two words?
translations.idiomatic: I fear that as they multiply day by day and swarm up the walls of advancement until they fill the court, the truly worthy will grow ever more distant. The harm and disaster that would follow—can it even be summed up in a word or two?

sentences.zh: 願觀《詩》、《書》之所任使，無速於小利近功，則王道可成矣。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will observe whom the Odes and Documents entrust and employ, and not hasten after petty profit and near-term achievement—then the kingly Way may be accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to look to whom the Odes and Documents appoint and employ, and not rush after petty gains and quick results—then the kingly Way may be achieved."

sentences.zh: 邵亢在樞府，無所建明，神宗語覺，欲出之，用陳升之以代。

translations.literal: Shao Kang was in the Bureau of Military Affairs and had accomplished nothing. Emperor Shenzong told Jue he wished to remove him and use Chen Shengzhi in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Kang held a post in the Bureau of Military Affairs but had accomplished nothing. The emperor told Jue he wanted to remove him and replace him with Chen Shengzhi.

sentences.zh: 覺退，即奏疏如所言。

translations.literal: Jue withdrew and immediately submitted a memorial stating what had been said.
translations.idiomatic: When Jue withdrew, he at once memorialized the court repeating what had been said.

sentences.zh: 神宗以為希旨，奪官兩級。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong considered this currying favor and stripped him of two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as pandering and reduced his rank by two grades.

sentences.zh: 執政曰：「諫官有出外，無降官之理。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers said: "Remonstrating officials may be sent outside the capital, but there is no precedent for demoting their rank."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers said, "Censorial remonstrators may be posted outside the capital, but there is no precedent for demoting their rank."

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「但降官，自不能住。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said: "Once his rank is reduced, he naturally cannot remain in office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Once his rank is lowered, he will not be able to stay in the post on his own."

sentences.zh: 覺連章丐去，云：「去歲有罰金御史，今茲有貶秩諫官，未聞罰金貶秩，而猶可居位者。」

translations.literal: Jue submitted repeated memorials begging to leave, saying: "Last year there was a censor fined; this year there is a remonstrator demoted in rank. I have never heard of one fined or demoted who could still hold office."
translations.idiomatic: Jue submitted memorial after memorial asking to be dismissed, writing, "Last year a censor was fined; this year a remonstrator is demoted. I have never heard of anyone fined or demoted who could still keep his post."

sentences.zh: 乃通判越州，復右正言，徙知通州。

translations.literal: He was then made vice-prefect of Yuezhou, restored to Right Rectifier, and transferred to serve as prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made vice-prefect of Yuezhou, restored to the post of Right Rectifier, and transferred to serve as prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，詔知諫院，同修起居注，知審官院。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, he was ordered to head the Remonstrance Bureau, co-edit the Diarists' Record, and direct the Bureau for Review of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xining era, he was ordered to head the Remonstrance Bureau, serve as co-editor of the court diary, and direct the Bureau for Review of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 王安石早與覺善，驟引用之，將援以為助。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi had long been on good terms with Jue and suddenly promoted him, intending to enlist his support.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi had long been friendly with Jue and suddenly promoted him, intending to win his help.

sentences.zh: 時呂惠卿用事，神宗詢於覺，對曰：「惠卿即辯而有才，過於人數等，特以為利之故，屈身於安石，安石不悟，臣竊以為憂。」

translations.literal: At the time Lü Huiqing was in power. Emperor Shenzong asked Jue about him. He replied: "Huiqing is indeed eloquent and talented, surpassing ordinary men by several degrees, but solely for profit's sake he humbles himself before Anshi—and Anshi does not perceive it. I privately take this as a cause for concern."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lü Huiqing was in power. When the emperor asked Jue about him, he answered, "Huiqing is indeed eloquent and talented—head and shoulders above the common run—but he defers to Anshi solely for gain, and Anshi does not see it. I cannot help but worry."

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「朕亦疑之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said: "I too have my doubts about him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have my doubts about him as well."

sentences.zh: 其後王、呂果交惡。

translations.literal: Afterward Wang and Lü indeed became mutually hostile.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Wang and Lü did indeed turn against each other.

sentences.zh: 青苗法行，首議者謂：「《周官》泉府，民之貸者，至輸息二十而五，國事之財用取具焉。」

translations.literal: When the Green Sprouts Law was implemented, its chief advocates said: "In the Offices of Zhou, the Treasury Office lent to the people, who paid interest up to twenty-five percent, and the state's financial needs were thereby supplied."
translations.idiomatic: When the Green Sprouts Law was put into effect, its chief advocates argued that under the Offices of Zhou the Treasury lent to the people at interest of twenty-five percent, and from this the state's revenue needs were fully met.

sentences.zh: 覺奏條其妄，曰：

translations.literal: Jue memorialized itemizing its errors and said:
translations.idiomatic: Jue memorialized the throne, listing its fallacies point by point, and said:

sentences.zh: 「成周賒貸，特以備民之緩急，不可徒與也，故以國服為之息。

translations.literal: "The lending of the Cheng-Zhou period was solely to meet the people's emergencies; it could not be given away freely, hence national mourning garments served as interest.
translations.idiomatic: "The loans of the Cheng-Zhou period were meant only to meet the people's emergencies—they could not be handed out for nothing, which is why interest was set in terms of mourning garments prescribed by the state.

sentences.zh: 然國服之息，說者不明。

translations.literal: Yet the interest in mourning garments—commentators have not made this clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what that interest in mourning garments actually meant, the commentators have never made clear.

sentences.zh: 鄭康成釋經，乃引王莽計贏受息，無過歲什一為據，不應周公取息，重於莽時。

translations.literal: When Zheng Xuan explained the classics, he cited Wang Mang's scheme of calculating profit and receiving interest, with nothing exceeding ten percent per year as his basis—yet the Duke of Zhou's interest should not have been heavier than in Mang's time.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Xuan explained the classics, he cited Wang Mang's profit-and-interest scheme, taking nothing more than ten percent per year as his evidence—yet it cannot be that the Duke of Zhou charged interest heavier than Wang Mang did.

sentences.zh: 況載師所任地，漆林之征特重，所以抑末作也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the territory assigned to the Market Master, the tax on lacquer groves was especially heavy, precisely to restrain secondary crafts.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the territory under the Market Master's charge, the tax on lacquer groves was especially heavy—precisely to restrain secondary industry.

sentences.zh: 今以農民乏絕，將補耕助斂，顧比末作而征之，可乎？

translations.literal: Now, because farmers are destitute, you would aid plowing and assist collection—yet would you levy taxes comparing them to secondary crafts? Is this permissible?
translations.idiomatic: Now, because farmers are destitute, you would aid plowing and assist tax collection—yet would you tax them at rates meant to restrain secondary industry? How can that be right?

sentences.zh: 國事取具，蓋謂泉府所領，若市之不售，貨之滯於民用，有買有予，並賒貸之法而舉之。

translations.literal: That state affairs were supplied means what the Treasury Office oversaw: when goods did not sell in the market or commodities stagnated for people's use, there were purchases and grants, and lending was carried out together with these methods.
translations.idiomatic: That state revenue was fully supplied refers to what the Treasury Office managed: when goods would not sell in the market or stock piled up beyond people's needs, there were purchases and grants, and lending was carried out alongside these measures.

sentences.zh: 儻專取具於泉府，則塚宰九賦，將安用邪？

translations.literal: If revenue were taken solely from the Treasury Office, what use would remain for the Chief Minister's nine levies?
translations.idiomatic: If revenue were to be drawn solely from the Treasury Office, what would become of the Chief Minister's nine levies?

sentences.zh: 聖世宜講求先王之法，不當取疑文虛說以圖治。

translations.literal: In a sage age one should seek out the methods of the former kings, and not take doubtful texts and empty theories as the basis for governing.
translations.idiomatic: In an enlightened age one should study the laws of the ancient kings, not seize on dubious passages and hollow theories to frame policy.

sentences.zh: 今老臣疏外而不見聽，輔臣遷延而不就職，門下執正而不行，諫官請罪而求去。

translations.literal: Now elderly ministers are kept at a distance and not heeded; chief ministers delay and do not take up their posts; the Gatekeepers hold to what is right but cannot act; remonstrators beg punishment and seek to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Now elderly ministers are pushed aside and ignored, chief ministers stall and refuse to take office, the Gatekeepers' righteous views go unheeded, and remonstrators beg to be punished and ask to resign.

sentences.zh: 臣誠恐奸邪之人，結黨連伍，乘眾情之洶洶，動搖朝廷，釣直干譽，非國家之福也。」

translations.literal: I truly fear that treacherous men will form factions and bands, ride the surge of popular agitation, shake the court, fish for reputation by feigning integrity, and bring no blessing to the state."
translations.idiomatic: I truly fear that wicked men will form factions, exploit the public uproar, shake the court, fish for reputation by posing as upright, and bring no blessing to the state."

sentences.zh: 安石覽之，怒，覺適以事詣中書，安石以語動之曰：「不意學士亦如此！」

translations.literal: Anshi read it and grew angry. Jue happened to come to the Secretariat on business. Anshi tried to sway him with words, saying: "I never expected the Academician to be like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Anshi read the memorial and was furious. Jue happened to visit the Secretariat on business, and Anshi tried to win him over, saying, "I never expected even you to go this far!"

sentences.zh: 始有逐覺意。

translations.literal: From this he first conceived the intention of driving Jue out.
translations.idiomatic: From that point he began to think of driving Jue out.

sentences.zh: 會曾公亮言畿縣散常平錢，有追呼抑配之擾，安石因請遣覺行視虛實。

translations.literal: It happened that Zeng Gongliang said that in the capital districts the distribution of Ever-Normal granary funds brought the disturbance of forced collection and compulsory allocation. Anshi therefore requested that Jue be sent to inspect the actual conditions.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zeng Gongliang reported that in the capital districts the distribution of Ever-Normal granary funds was causing forced collection and compulsory allocation. Anshi seized the chance to ask that Jue be sent to investigate on the spot.

sentences.zh: 覺既受命，復奏疏辭行，且言：「如陳留一縣，前後曉示，情願請錢，卒無一人至者，故陳留不散一錢。

translations.literal: Once Jue had received the order, he again submitted a memorial declining to go, and said: "Take Chenliu County as an example: notices were issued repeatedly, yet not a single person willing to borrow came forward, so Chenliu did not distribute a single coin.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jue had his orders, he memorialized again asking to be excused from the mission, and said, "In Chenliu County, for instance, proclamations were issued again and again inviting people to borrow—but in the end not one person came forward, so Chenliu did not distribute a single coin.

sentences.zh: 以此見民實不願與官中相交。

translations.literal: From this one sees that the people truly do not wish to deal with the government.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the people truly do not wish to deal with the government.

sentences.zh: 所有體量，望賜寢罷。」

translations.literal: As for the investigation I have been assigned, I pray it may be granted rest and cancellation."
translations.idiomatic: As for the investigation I have been assigned, I beg that it be canceled."

sentences.zh: 遂以覺為反覆，出知廣德軍，徙湖州。

translations.literal: He was then deemed inconstant and sent out as military prefect of Guangde, then transferred to Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then judged to be inconsistent and sent out as military prefect of Guangde, then transferred to Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 松江堤沒，水為民患。

translations.literal: The Song River embankment was breached and the water became a scourge to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Song River embankment had collapsed, and flooding plagued the people.

sentences.zh: 覺易以石，高丈餘，長百里，堤下化為良田。

translations.literal: Jue replaced it with stone, more than ten feet high and a hundred li long; below the dike the land became fertile fields.
translations.idiomatic: Jue rebuilt it in stone, more than ten feet high and a hundred li long, and the land below the dike was turned into rich farmland.

sentences.zh: 徙廬州，改右司諫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Luzhou and changed to Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Luzhou and promoted to Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以祖母喪求解官，下太常議，不可，詔知潤州，覺已持喪矣。

translations.literal: On his grandmother's death he requested leave from office. The matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, which ruled it impermissible. He was ordered to serve as prefect of Runzhou, but Jue was already observing mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandmother died he asked to resign. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices was consulted and ruled against it; he was ordered to serve as prefect of Runzhou, but Jue was already in mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，知蘇州，徙福州。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he served as prefect of Suzhou and was transferred to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he became prefect of Suzhou and was later transferred to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 閩俗厚於婚喪，其費無藝。

translations.literal: Fujian custom was lavish in weddings and funerals, with expenses beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian custom was extravagant in weddings and funerals, with costs beyond all bounds.

sentences.zh: 覺裁為中法，使資裝無得過百千。

translations.literal: Jue set a standard regulation, permitting dowry and funeral goods to exceed no more than a hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Jue imposed a standard regulation capping dowries and funeral expenses at no more than a hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 令下，嫁娶以百數，葬埋之費亦率減什伍。

translations.literal: Once the order was issued, wedding expenses fell to the hundreds, and burial costs likewise were reduced by about half.
translations.idiomatic: Once the order took effect, wedding costs fell to the hundreds, and burial expenses were likewise cut by roughly half.

sentences.zh: 連徙亳、揚、徐州。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to Bo, Yang, and Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred in succession to Bo, Yang, and Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 徐多盜，捕得殺人者五，其一僅勝衣，疑而訊之，曰：「我耕於野，與甲遇，強以梃與我，半夜挾我東，使候諸門，不知其他也。」

translations.literal: Xuzhou had many bandits. Five murderers were captured; one was barely taller than his clothes. Doubting him, Jue questioned him. He said: "I was plowing in the fields when I met a soldier who forced a club on me. At midnight he dragged me east and made me wait at the gates—I know nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou had many bandits. Five murderers were captured; one was scarcely taller than his clothes. Jue questioned him in suspicion, and the boy said, "I was plowing in the fields when I met a soldier who forced a club into my hands. At midnight he dragged me east and made me wait at the gates—I know nothing more."

sentences.zh: 問吏：「法何如？」

translations.literal: He asked the clerks: "What does the law prescribe?"
translations.idiomatic: Jue asked the clerks, "What does the law prescribe?"

translations.literal: They said: "Death."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Death."

sentences.zh: 覺止誅其首，後遂為例。

translations.literal: Jue executed only the ringleader, and this afterward became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Jue executed only the ringleader, and this afterward became precedent.

sentences.zh: 進吏部侍郎，領右選，在選萬五千員，闕才五之二，至有三年不得調者。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and headed the Right Selection. Those awaiting appointment numbered fifteen thousand; vacancies were only two-fifths of posts, and some waited three years without assignment.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and headed the Right Selection Board. Fifteen thousand candidates were waiting for posts, but vacancies amounted to only two-fifths of the posts available, and some waited three years without an assignment.

sentences.zh: 覺請自軍功、保甲進者補指使，宗室袒免從員外置，一日得闕數千。

translations.literal: Jue requested that those advancing through military merit and the baojia system be appointed as envoys, and that imperial clansmen with partial mourning privileges be placed from outside the regular quota—in one day several thousand vacancies were filled.
translations.idiomatic: Jue proposed that men advanced through military merit and the baojia system be appointed as envoys, and that imperial clansmen with partial mourning privileges be placed from outside the regular quota—in a single day several thousand vacancies were filled.

sentences.zh: 改主左選，請磨勘歲以百人為限。

translations.literal: He was changed to head the Left Selection and requested that annual merit reviews be limited to a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to head the Left Selection Board and asked that annual merit reviews be capped at a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 擢御史中丞，數月，以疾請罷，除龍圖閣學士兼侍講，提舉醴泉觀，求舒州靈仙觀以歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief. After several months he begged to resign on account of illness and was made Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall with concurrent duty as Lecturer, put in charge of the Liquan Abbey, and sought the Lingxian Abbey in Shuzhou to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief. After several months he asked to resign on account of illness and was made Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall with concurrent duty as court lecturer, placed in charge of the Liquan Abbey, and sought the Lingxian Abbey in Shuzhou in order to retire home.

sentences.zh: 哲宗遣使存勞，賜白金五百兩。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong sent envoys to inquire after his welfare and bestowed five hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong sent envoys to inquire after his health and bestowed five hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 覺有德量，為王安石所逐。

translations.literal: Jue had moral stature and was driven out by Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Jue possessed moral stature and had been driven out by Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 安石退居鍾山，覺枉駕道舊，為從容累夕；

translations.literal: When Anshi retired to Zhong Mountain, Jue made a special trip to renew old friendship and spent several relaxed evenings with him;
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi retired to Mount Zhong, Jue made a special trip to renew their old friendship and spent several relaxed evenings with him;

sentences.zh: 迨其死，又作文以誄，談者稱之。

translations.literal: when he died, Jue again composed a eulogy, and commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: when Anshi died, Jue composed a funeral elegy as well, which commentators praised.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，以覺為元祐黨，奪職追兩官。

translations.literal: During the Shaosheng era he was classed as a Yuanyou partisan; his posts were stripped and two ranks were retroactively removed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era he was branded a Yuanyou partisan; his posts were stripped and two ranks were retroactively removed.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，復官職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, his offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong took the throne, his offices were restored.

sentences.zh: 有文集、奏議六十卷，《春秋傳》十五卷。

translations.literal: He left collected writings and memorials in sixty juan, and a Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals in fifteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings and memorials in sixty juan, and a Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals in fifteen juan.

sentences.zh: 弟覽。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Lan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Lan.

sentences.zh: 弟 覽

translations.literal: Younger brother Lan
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Lan

sentences.zh: 覽，字傅師。

translations.literal: Lan, style name Fushi.
translations.idiomatic: Lan, courtesy name Fushi.

sentences.zh: 擢第，知尉氏縣。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations and served as magistrate of Weishi County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil examinations and served as magistrate of Weishi County.

sentences.zh: 有屯將遇下虐，士卒謀因大閱殺之以叛。

translations.literal: A garrison commander treated his subordinates cruelly, and the soldiers plotted to kill him during the grand review and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: A garrison commander was cruel to his men, and the soldiers plotted to kill him during the grand review and rise in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 覽聞之，馳往，士猶群語不顧，覽呼諭之曰：「將誠無狀，然天子何負汝輩，乃欲致族滅邪？」

translations.literal: Lan heard of it and galloped there. The soldiers were still talking in groups and paid no heed. Lan called out to instruct them: "The commander is indeed vile, but what wrong has the Son of Heaven done you, that you would bring extermination on your clans?"
translations.idiomatic: Lan heard of it and galloped to the scene. The men were still talking in groups and ignored him until he called out, "The commander may be vile, but what has the Son of Heaven done to you, that you would bring extermination on your families?"

sentences.zh: 皆感謝去就列。

translations.literal: They all thanked him with emotion and returned to their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: They all thanked him with emotion and returned to their ranks.

sentences.zh: 屯將徐至，覽命吏趣具奏，眾意遂安。

translations.literal: The garrison commander arrived slowly. Lan ordered clerks to hurry preparation of a memorial, and the men's minds were calmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the commander arrived at last, Lan ordered his clerks to prepare a memorial at once, and the men's minds were set at ease.

sentences.zh: 神宗壯其材，以為司農主簿。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong admired his talent and appointed him Registrar of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong admired his talent and appointed him Registrar of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 舒亶判寺且兼諫院，欲引覽自助，覽拒不答。

translations.literal: Shu Dan judged the ministry and concurrently held the Remonstrance Bureau; he wished to draw Lan in to assist him, but Lan refused to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Dan served as judge of the ministry and concurrently held the Remonstrance Bureau; he wished to draw Lan in as an ally, but Lan refused to respond.

sentences.zh: 亶怒，用帳籍違事劾之。

translations.literal: Dan grew angry and impeached him on a charge of violating regulations in the account books.
translations.idiomatic: Dan grew angry and impeached him for irregularities in the account books.

sentences.zh: 出提舉利州、湖南常平，改京西轉運判官，入為右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He was sent out as intendant of Ever-Normal granaries for Lizhou and Hunan, changed to transport-assessor of the Jingxi circuit, and entered the capital as Right Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as intendant of Ever-Normal granaries for Lizhou and Hunan, then became transport-assessor of the Jingxi circuit, and entered the capital as Right Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 荊湖開疆，命往相其便。

translations.literal: When Jinghu opened new territory, he was ordered to go and assess what would be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinghu opened new territory, he was ordered to go and assess what would be advantageous.

sentences.zh: 覽言：「沅州所招溪洞百三十，宜從本郡隨事要束，勿建官置戍以為民困。

translations.literal: Lan said: "The hundred and thirty stream-cave groups recruited by Yuanzhou should be bound according to local conditions by their native prefectures—do not establish officials and garrisons to burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: Lan said, "The hundred and thirty stream-cave groups recruited by Yuanzhou should be managed according to local conditions by their native prefectures—do not establish officials and garrisons to burden the people.

sentences.zh: 自誠州至融江口，可通西廣鹽，以省北道餉餽。」

translations.literal: From Chenzhou to the mouth of the Rong River, Western Guang salt could be brought through to save northern-route supply transport."
translations.idiomatic: From Chenzhou to the mouth of the Rong River, Western Guang salt could be brought through, saving supply transport along the northern route."

sentences.zh: 悉從之。

translations.literal: All was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted all of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 使還，為河東、河北轉運副使，加直龍圖閣，歷知河中應天府、江淮發運使。

translations.literal: On his return from the mission he became Vice Transport Commissioner for Hedong and Hebei, was given the rank of Direct Dragon Diagram Courtier, and served in succession as prefect of Hezhong and Yingtianfu and as transport commissioner for the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became Vice Transport Commissioner for Hedong and Hebei, was given the rank of Direct Dragon Diagram Courtier, and served in succession as prefect of Hezhong and Yingtianfu and as transport commissioner for the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 進寶文閣待制，由桂徙廣，又改渭州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Baowen Hall, transferred from Gui to Guang, and then changed to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Baowen Hall, transferred from Gui to Guang, and then reassigned to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 夏人入邊，檄大將苗履禦之，履稱疾移告，立按正其罪，竄諸房陵，轅門肅然。

translations.literal: When the Tangut Xi Xia invaded the border, he issued orders to the great general Miao Lü to repel them. Lü claimed illness and requested leave. Lan immediately investigated and established his guilt, banishing him to Fangling; discipline at the headquarters gate was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut Xi Xia raided the border, he ordered the great general Miao Lü to repel them. Lü claimed illness and asked for leave. Lan immediately investigated, established his guilt, and banished him to Fangling; discipline at headquarters was restored at once.

sentences.zh: 召知開封府，至則拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as prefect of Kaifeng; upon arrival he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as prefect of Kaifeng; upon arrival he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 與蔡京論役法不合，以龍圖閣直學士知太原。

translations.literal: He disagreed with Cai Jing on the corvée law and was made Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with Cai Jing over the corvée law and was made Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 夏人據橫山，並河為寨，秦、晉之路皆塞。

translations.literal: The Xi Xia held Heng Mountain and built fortresses along the Yellow River; the routes of Qin and Jin were all blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi Xia held Heng Mountain and built fortresses along the Yellow River; the routes linking Qin and Jin were all cut off.

sentences.zh: 覽謀復取葭蘆戍，阻險不得前。

translations.literal: Lan planned to recover the Jialu garrison but was blocked by difficult terrain and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Lan planned to recover the Jialu garrison but was blocked by difficult terrain and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 夏人數萬屯境上，覽下令吾兵少，須滿五萬。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of Xi Xia troops camped on the border. Lan ordered: "Our troops are few—we must have a full fifty thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of thousands of Xi Xia troops camped on the border. Lan ordered, "Our forces are too few—we must have a full fifty thousand men."

sentences.zh: 及西夏人聞而濟師，覽不為動，相持益久，忽令具糗糧，嚴兵械，曰：「敵至矣！」

translations.literal: When the Xi Xia heard this and crossed the river with their army, Lan was unmoved. The standoff grew longer. Suddenly he ordered provisions prepared and weapons readied, saying: "The enemy has come!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Xi Xia heard this and crossed the river with their army, Lan did not stir. The standoff dragged on until suddenly he ordered provisions prepared and weapons readied, crying, "The enemy is here!"

sentences.zh: 居數日，果大入，覽奮擊敗之，遂城葭蘆而還。

translations.literal: After several days they indeed launched a major invasion. Lan struck back vigorously and defeated them, then fortified Jialu and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After several days they did launch a major invasion. Lan struck back hard and routed them, then fortified Jialu and returned.

sentences.zh: 策勳，加樞密直學士。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the rank of Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was given the rank of Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 覽雖立邊功，議論多觸執政，屢遭絀削，歷知河南、永興，徙成都。

translations.literal: Although Lan had won border merit, his opinions often offended those in power and he suffered repeated demotions, serving in succession as prefect of Henan and Yongxing and transferred to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Although Lan had won distinction on the frontier, his opinions often offended those in power and he suffered repeated demotions, serving in succession as prefect of Henan and Yongxing before being transferred to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 辭不行，降為寶文閣待制。

translations.literal: He declined to go and was demoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Baowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post and was demoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Baowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 李常，字公擇，南康建昌人。

translations.literal: Li Chang, style name Gongze, was a native of Jianchang in Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang, courtesy name Gongze, was a native of Jianchang in Nankang.

sentences.zh: 少讀書廬山白石僧舍。

translations.literal: In youth he studied at the White Stone monk's lodge on Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied at the White Stone monk's lodge on Mount Lu.

sentences.zh: 既擢第，留所抄書九千卷，名舍曰「李氏山房」。

translations.literal: After passing the examinations he left behind nine thousand juan of copied books and named the lodge the "Li Family Mountain Studio."
translations.idiomatic: After passing the examinations he left behind nine thousand juan of copied books at the lodge, which he named the Li Family Mountain Studio.

sentences.zh: 調江州判官、宣州觀察推官。

translations.literal: He was assigned as judge of Jiangzhou and investigating clerk of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as judge of Jiangzhou and investigating clerk of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 發運使楊佐將薦改秩，常推其友劉琦，佐曰：「世無此風久矣。」

translations.literal: The transport commissioner Yang Zuo was about to recommend him for a change in rank; Chang recommended his friend Liu Qi. Zuo said, "This kind of conduct has been absent from the world for a long time."
translations.idiomatic: When Transport Commissioner Yang Zuo was preparing to recommend Li Chang for promotion, Chang instead put forward his friend Liu Qi. Zuo said, "This sort of selfless conduct has been rare in the world for a long time."

sentences.zh: 並薦之。

translations.literal: He recommended both of them.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended both men.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，為秘閣校理。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era, he served as a collator in the Secret Repository.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xining reign, he was appointed collator in the Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 王安石與之善，以為三司條例檢詳官，改右正言、知諫院。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi was on good terms with him and appointed him examining officer for the Three Offices Regulations, changed his title to Right Remonstrance Counselor, and made him director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi, who was friendly with him, made him examining officer for the Three Offices Regulations, promoted him to Right Remonstrance Counselor, and put him in charge of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 安石立新法，常預議，不欲青苗收息。

translations.literal: When Anshi established the New Policies, Chang participated in the deliberations but did not wish to collect interest on Green Sprouts loans.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi launched the New Policies, Chang took part in the discussions but opposed collecting interest on the Green Sprouts loans.

sentences.zh: 至是，疏言：「條例司始建，已致中外之議。

translations.literal: At this time he submitted a memorial saying, "Since the Regulations Commission was first established, it has already provoked debate inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he submitted a memorial stating, "From the moment the Regulations Commission was created, it has already stirred controversy throughout the court and the country.

sentences.zh: 至於均輸、青苗，斂散取息，傅會經義，人且大駭，何異王莽猥析《周官》片言，以流毒天下！」

translations.literal: As for Equal Transport and Green Sprouts—gathering and dispersing to collect interest, forcing a fit with classical meaning—the people will be greatly alarmed. How is this different from Wang Mang vulgarly splitting isolated phrases from the Rites of Zhou to spread poison throughout the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: When it comes to Equal Transport and Green Sprouts—stockpiling and releasing grain to charge interest while twisting the classics to justify it—the people will be terrified. What difference is there between this and Wang Mang wrenching stray lines from the Rites of Zhou to poison the whole empire?"

sentences.zh: 安石見之，遣所親密諭意，常不為止。

translations.literal: When Anshi saw it, he sent a close associate to convey his wishes privately, but Chang would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi read the memorial, he sent a trusted confidant to hint at his wishes in private, but Chang refused to back down.

sentences.zh: 又言：「州縣散常平錢，實不出本，勒民出息。」

translations.literal: He also said, "The prefectures and counties are dispersing Ever-Normal Granary funds, yet in reality the principal is never released, while the people are compelled to pay interest."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Prefectures and counties are lending out Ever-Normal Granary funds, but in practice the principal never reaches the people, while they are still forced to pay interest."

sentences.zh: 神宗詰安石，安石請令常具官吏主名，常以非諫官體，落校理，通判滑州。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong questioned Anshi. Anshi requested that Chang provide the full names of the officials involved. Chang, on the grounds that this was not proper Remonstrance Bureau protocol, was stripped of his collator post and made vice prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong pressed Anshi for an explanation. Anshi asked that Chang supply the names of the officials responsible. Chang argued that this was not how a remonstrance official should proceed, and as a result he was removed as collator and sent out as vice prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘復職，知鄂州，徙湖、齊二州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was restored to office, became prefect of Ezhou, and was transferred to the prefectures of Hu and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After a little over a year he was reinstated, served as prefect of Ezhou, and was later transferred to Hu and Qi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 齊多盜，論報無虛日。

translations.literal: In Qi there were many bandits, and there was not a day without trials and sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had many bandits, and hardly a day passed without trials and verdicts.

sentences.zh: 常得黠盜，刺為兵，使在麾下，盡知囊括處，悉發屋破柱，拔其根株，半歲間，誅七百人，奸無所匿。

translations.literal: Chang captured crafty bandits, tattooed them as soldiers, and kept them under his command. They knew all the hiding places of loot; he thoroughly searched houses and broke pillars, uprooting them at the root. Within half a year, seven hundred were executed, and evildoers had nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: Chang captured clever bandits, marked them as soldiers, and kept them in his service. They knew every stash of stolen goods, so he had houses torn apart and pillars broken until the whole network was uprooted. Within six months he had executed seven hundred men, and criminals had nowhere left to hide.

sentences.zh: 徙淮南西路提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be judicial intendant of Huainan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as judicial intendant on Huainan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 元豐六年，召為太常少卿，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng, he was recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng he was recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，改吏部，進戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, he was moved to the Ministry of Personnel and advanced to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong came to the throne, Chang was shifted to the Ministry of Personnel and then promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 或疑其少幹局，慮不勝任，質於司馬光。

translations.literal: Some doubted that he lacked executive ability and worried he would not be up to the task; they asked Sima Guang about it.
translations.idiomatic: Some questioned whether he had enough practical ability and feared he might not be equal to the post, so they put the matter to Sima Guang.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「用常主邦計，則人知朝廷不急於征利，聚斂少息矣。」

translations.literal: Guang said, "If Chang is put in charge of state finances, people will know the court is not eager to pursue profit, and extortionate collection will somewhat cease."
translations.idiomatic: Guang replied, "If Chang is placed in charge of the nation's finances, people will understand that the court is not desperate for revenue, and the pressure for harsh taxation will ease."

sentences.zh: 常轉對，上七事，曰崇廉恥、存鄉舉、別守宰、廢貪贓、審疑獄、擇儒師、修役法。

translations.literal: Chang addressed the throne in rotation, presenting seven matters: to honor integrity and shame, preserve local recommendation, distinguish prefects and magistrates, abolish corruption, carefully review doubtful cases, select Confucian teachers, and revise corvée law.
translations.idiomatic: In a rotating audience with the emperor, Chang presented seven proposals: promote integrity and shame, preserve local recommendation, distinguish good from bad prefects and magistrates, eliminate corruption, review doubtful legal cases, choose worthy Confucian teachers, and reform the corvée system.

sentences.zh: 時役法差、免二科未定，常謂：「法無新陳，便民者良；

translations.literal: At the time the two categories of corvée law—assignment and exemption—were not settled. Chang said, "In law there is no old and new; what benefits the people is good;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the two forms of corvée law, assignment and exemption, had not yet been settled. Chang argued, "Laws are not about old versus new; what serves the people is best.

sentences.zh: 論無彼己，可久者確。

translations.literal: In discussion there should be no 'them and us'; what can last is firm.
translations.idiomatic: Debate should not be about sides; what can endure is what matters.

sentences.zh: 今使民俱出貲則貧者難辦，俱出力則富者難堪，各從其願，則可久爾。」

translations.literal: If all the people are made to pay money together, the poor cannot manage it; if all are made to provide labor, the rich cannot bear it. Let each follow his wish, and it can be enduring."
translations.idiomatic: If everyone is required to pay in cash, the poor cannot afford it; if everyone must provide labor, the wealthy cannot endure it. Let each person choose according to his means, and the system can last."

sentences.zh: 乃折衷條上之。

translations.literal: He then submitted a compromise proposal item by item.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a balanced compromise, item by item.

sentences.zh: 赦恩，蠲市易逋負不滿二百緡者，常請息過其數亦勿取。

translations.literal: In an amnesty, debts owed on the Market Exchange below two hundred strings were cancelled; Chang requested that even interest exceeding that amount should not be collected.
translations.idiomatic: During an amnesty, Market Exchange arrears under two hundred strings of cash were forgiven; Chang asked that interest above that amount also not be collected.

sentences.zh: 拜御史中丞，兼侍讀，加龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Censor-in-Chief, concurrently Reader-in-Attendance, with the added title of Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Pictures.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Censor-in-Chief and concurrent Reader-in-Attendance, with the added rank of Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Pictures.

sentences.zh: 論取士，請分詩賦、經義為兩科，以盡所長。

translations.literal: On the matter of selecting scholars, he requested dividing poetry-and-prose composition and classical-meaning examinations into two categories, so each might fully display his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: On selecting officials, he proposed splitting the poetry-and-prose and classical-meaning examinations into two separate tracks so that each candidate could show his full strengths.

sentences.zh: 初，河決小吳，議者欲自孫村口導還故處，及是役興，常言：「京東、河北饑困，不宜導河。」

translations.literal: Previously the Yellow River breached at Xiaowu. Discussants wished to divert it back to its old course from Suncun Estuary. When this labor project was launched, Chang said, "Jingdong and Hebei are suffering famine and hardship; it is not appropriate to divert the river."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Yellow River had broken through at Xiaowu, and officials proposed diverting it back to its old channel from Suncun Estuary. When that project was launched, Chang said, "Jingdong and Hebei are already suffering famine and hardship; this is no time to redirect the river."

sentences.zh: 詔罷之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the project halted.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict halted the project.

sentences.zh: 諫官劉安世以吳處厚繳蔡確詩為謗訕，因力攻確。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Liu Anshi, taking Wu Chuhou's submission of Cai Que's poems as slander, therefore vigorously attacked Que.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Liu Anshi treated Wu Chuhou's submission of Cai Que's poems as defamation and launched a fierce attack on Que.

sentences.zh: 常上疏論以詩罪確，非所以厚風俗。

translations.literal: Chang submitted a memorial arguing that punishing Que on the basis of poetry was not a way to strengthen custom.
translations.idiomatic: Chang submitted a memorial arguing that convicting Que on the basis of poetry was no way to strengthen public morals.

sentences.zh: 安世並劾常，徙兵部尚書，辭不拜，出知鄧州。

translations.literal: Liu Anshi also impeached Chang; he was transferred to Minister of War, declined the appointment, and went out as prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Anshi also impeached Chang, who was transferred to Minister of War. Chang declined the appointment and went out to serve as prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙成都，行次陝，暴卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: Transferred to Chengdu; while traveling, passing through Shan, he died suddenly, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chengdu, but while en route and passing through Shan, he died suddenly at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 有文集、奏議六十卷，《詩傳》十卷，《元祐會計錄》三十卷。

translations.literal: He left collected works and memorials in sixty volumes, a Commentary on the Poetry in ten volumes, and the Yuanyou Fiscal Records in thirty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included sixty volumes of collected works and memorials, ten volumes of a Commentary on the Poetry, and thirty volumes of the Yuanyou Fiscal Records.

sentences.zh: 常長孫覺一歲，始與覺齊名，俱受知於呂公著。

translations.literal: Chang was one year older than his eldest grandson Sun Jue; at first he and Jue were equally renowned, and both won the favor of Lü Gongzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was one year older than his eldest grandson Sun Jue. At first he and Jue were equally famous, and both enjoyed the patronage of Lü Gongzhu.

sentences.zh: 其論議趣舍，大略多同，所終官職又同，其死，先後一夕云。

translations.literal: Their views and choices in debate were for the most part similar; the final offices they held were also the same, and their deaths were said to have been one day apart.
translations.idiomatic: Their views and political choices were largely the same, they ended in the same final offices, and it was said that they died only a day apart.

sentences.zh: 孔文仲

translations.literal: Kong Wenzhong
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wenzhong

sentences.zh: 孔文仲，字經父，臨江新喻人。

translations.literal: Kong Wenzhong, style name Jingfu, was a native of Xinyu in Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wenzhong, courtesy name Jingfu, was a native of Xinyu in Linjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性狷直，寡言笑，少刻苦問學，號博洽。

translations.literal: His nature was blunt and upright; he spoke little and laughed little. From youth he studied arduously and was known as broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt and upright by nature, spoke little, and rarely laughed. From youth he studied with great diligence and was known for his wide learning.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，南省考官呂夏卿，稱其詞賦贍麗，策論深博，文勢似荀卿、楊雄，白主司，擢第一。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination. The metropolitan examiner Lü Xiaqing praised his fu and shi as rich and beautiful, his policy essays as deep and broad, and his literary force as resembling Xun Qing and Yang Xiong; he reported to the chief examiner, and Wenzhong was placed first.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination. Metropolitan examiner Lü Xiaqing praised his poetry and prose as rich and polished, his policy essays as deep and broad, and his literary power as reminiscent of Xunzi and Yang Xiong. Lü reported this to the chief examiner, and Wenzhong was ranked first.

sentences.zh: 調餘杭尉。

translations.literal: He was assigned as assistant magistrate of Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant magistrate of Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 恬介自守，不事請謁。

translations.literal: Quiet and principled in self-conduct, he did not engage in solicitations and visits.
translations.idiomatic: Calm and principled, he kept to himself and never paid court to the powerful.

sentences.zh: 轉運使在杭，召與議事，事已，馳歸不詣府。

translations.literal: When the transport commissioner was in Hangzhou, he summoned Wenzhong to discuss affairs; when the business was done, Wenzhong raced home and did not call at the commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: When the transport commissioner was in Hangzhou, he summoned Wenzhong to discuss official business. Once the matter was finished, Wenzhong hurried home and never called at the commissioner's office.

sentences.zh: 人問之，曰：「吾於府無事也。」

translations.literal: When people asked him about it, he said, "I have no business with the commissioner's office."
translations.idiomatic: When people asked him about this, he said, "I have no further business with the commissioner's office."

sentences.zh: 再轉台州推官。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to be investigating officer of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to serve as investigating officer in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，翰林學士范鎮以制舉薦，對策九千餘言，力論王安石所建理財、訓兵之法為非是，宋敏求第為異等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining, Hanlin academician Fan Zhen recommended him through the decree examination; his response ran to over nine thousand characters, forcefully arguing that Wang Anshi's fiscal and military training methods were wrong. Song Minqiu ranked him in the exceptional grade.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xining era, Hanlin Academician Fan Zhen recommended him for the decree examination. His response ran to more than nine thousand characters and forcefully argued that Wang Anshi's fiscal and military training policies were mistaken. Song Minqiu ranked him in the exceptional grade.

sentences.zh: 安石怒，啟神宗，御批罷歸故官。

translations.literal: Anshi was angry and reported to Shenzong; an imperial rescript dismissed him and sent him back to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was furious and reported the matter to Shenzong, who issued an imperial rescript dismissing Wenzhong and sending him back to his former post.

sentences.zh: 齊恢、孫固封還御批，韓維、陳薦、孫永皆力言文仲不當黜，五上章，不聽。

translations.literal: Qi Hui and Sun Gu returned the rescript sealed; Han Wei, Chen Jian, and Sun Yong all strongly argued that Wenzhong should not be dismissed—five memorials in all—but they were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Hui and Sun Gu returned the rescript unopened. Han Wei, Chen Jian, and Sun Yong all strongly argued that Wenzhong should not be dismissed, submitting five memorials in all, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 范鎮又言：「文仲草茅疏遠，不識忌諱。

translations.literal: Fan Zhen also said, "Wenzhong is a rustic far from court, ignorant of taboos.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen added, "Wenzhong is a commoner far from court and does not know what must not be said.

sentences.zh: 且以直言求之，而又罪之，恐為聖明之累。」

translations.literal: Moreover, since frank speech was sought from him, yet he is punished for it—I fear this may be a blemish on the sage ruler's reign."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court asked for frank speech and now punishes him for it. I fear this will reflect badly on Your Majesty's enlightened rule."

sentences.zh: 亦不聽。

translations.literal: This too was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: This appeal too went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 蘇頌歎曰：「方朝廷求賢如饑渴，有如此人而不見錄，豈其論太高而難合邪？

translations.literal: Su Song sighed and said, "Just when the court seeks the worthy as if starving and thirsty, there is such a man yet he is not employed—is his doctrine too lofty to fit?
translations.idiomatic: Su Song sighed and said, "Just when the court is seeking talent as if starving and thirsty, there is a man like this who goes unrecognized. Is his doctrine too lofty to be accepted?

sentences.zh: 言太激而取怨邪？」

translations.literal: Or is it that his words were too sharp and drew resentment?"
translations.idiomatic: Or were his words too sharp and therefore drew resentment?"

sentences.zh: 吳充為相，欲置之館閣，又有忌之者，僅得國子直講。

translations.literal: When Wu Chong became chief councilor, he wished to place Wenzhong in the Hanlin archives, but there were those who envied him; he obtained only the post of lecturer in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Chong became chief councilor, he wanted to place Wenzhong in the Hanlin archives, but rivals blocked the move, and Wenzhong received only the post of lecturer in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 學者方用王氏經義進取，文仲不習其書，換為三班主簿，出通判保德軍。

translations.literal: Scholars at the time were using Wang's classical interpretations to advance; Wenzhong had not studied those texts, so he was exchanged for a clerk in the Three Ranks and sent out as vice prefect of Baode Army.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars at the time were advancing through Wang Anshi's commentaries, but Wenzhong had not studied those texts, so he was swapped out for a clerk in the Three Ranks and sent out as vice prefect of Baode Army.

sentences.zh: 時征西夏，眾數十萬皆道境上，久不解，邊人厭苦。

translations.literal: At the time the campaign against Western Xia was underway; several hundred thousand troops lined the border routes; the campaign dragged on without resolution, and border people were weary and suffering.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the empire was campaigning against Western Xia. Several hundred thousand men clogged the border routes, the war dragged on without end, and the frontier population was exhausted and miserable.

sentences.zh: 文仲陳三不便，曰：「大兵未出，而丁夫預集；

translations.literal: Wenzhong presented three inconveniences, saying, "The great army has not yet moved out, yet corvée laborers are pre-assembled;
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong presented three objections, saying, "The main army has not yet marched out, yet corvée laborers are already being assembled;

sentences.zh: 河東雇夫，勞民而損費；

translations.literal: hiring laborers in Hedong exhausts the people and wastes funds;
translations.idiomatic: hiring laborers in Hedong exhausts the people and wastes money;

sentences.zh: 諸路出兵，首尾不相應。

translations.literal: troops dispatched from various circuits do not coordinate from head to tail.
translations.idiomatic: and troops sent out from the various circuits fail to coordinate with one another.

sentences.zh: 虞、夏、商、周之盛，未嘗無外侮，然懷柔制禦之要，不在彼而在此也。」

translations.literal: Even at the height of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou, there were never lacking external threats; yet the essentials of soothing and controlling them lie not over there but here."
translations.idiomatic: Even at the height of the Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties, external threats were never absent, yet the key to soothing and controlling them lay not over there but here at home."

sentences.zh: 元祐初，哲宗召為秘書省校書郎，進禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, Zhezong summoned him as collator in the Secretariat and promoted him to Outer Office Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanyou era, Emperor Zhezong summoned him as collator in the Secretariat and then promoted him to Outer Office Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 有言：「皇族唯楊、荊二王得稱皇叔，餘宜各系其祖，若唐人稱諸王孫之比。」

translations.literal: Someone proposed, "Among the imperial clan, only the Princes of Yang and Jing should be styled Imperial Uncles; the rest should each be tied to their ancestors, like the Tang practice of calling them grandsons of the princes."
translations.idiomatic: Someone proposed that among the imperial clan only the Princes of Yang and Jing should be styled Imperial Uncles, while the rest should be linked to their ancestors, as in the Tang practice of calling them grandsons of the princes.

sentences.zh: 文仲曰：「上新即位，宜廣敦睦之義，不應疏間骨肉。」

translations.literal: Wenzhong said, "The emperor has newly ascended the throne; he should broadly extend the meaning of kinship harmony and not estrange blood relations."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong replied, "The emperor has just ascended the throne and should broadly extend the bonds of kinship harmony, not create distance among members of the imperial family."

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人，擢左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was moved to Diarist and promoted to Left Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Diarist and promoted to Left Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee.

sentences.zh: 日食七月朔，上疏條五事，曰：「邪說亂正道、小人乘君子、遠服侮中國、斜封奪公論、人臣輕國命，宜察此以消厭兆祥。」

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month there was a solar eclipse; he submitted a memorial listing five matters, saying, "Corrupt doctrines disrupting the orthodox Way, petty men riding over gentlemen, distant subjects despising China, backdoor letters seizing public discourse, and ministers treating the state's mandate lightly—these should be examined to dispel ominous signs."
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month there was a solar eclipse. He submitted a memorial listing five problems: corrupt doctrines undermining the orthodox Way, petty men prevailing over gentlemen, distant peoples scorning China, sealed back-channel petitions overriding public debate, and officials treating the state's mandate lightly. These, he said, should be examined in order to dispel the omen.

sentences.zh: 論青苗、免役，首困天下，保甲、保馬、茶鹽之法，為遣螫留蠹。

translations.literal: Discussing Green Sprouts and Exemption Corvée, he said they first exhausted the realm; the Baojia, Baoma, tea, and salt laws left lingering stings and leftover pests.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the Green Sprouts and Exemption Corvée policies had first exhausted the empire, while the Baojia, Baoma, tea, and salt laws left behind stings and lingering corruption.

sentences.zh: 改中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was changed to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 三年，同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the third year, he served as associate chief examiner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his service he served as associate chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 文仲先有寒疾，及是，晝夜不廢職。

translations.literal: Wenzhong had had a cold ailment from before; at this time, day and night he did not neglect his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong had long suffered from a chronic cold ailment, but during the examinations he never neglected his duties, working day and night.

sentences.zh: 同院以其形瘵，勸之先出，或居別寢。

translations.literal: Colleagues in the same office, seeing his consumptive appearance, urged him to leave early or stay in separate quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues in the same office, seeing how wasted he looked, urged him to leave early or at least sleep in separate quarters.

sentences.zh: 謝曰：「居官則任其責，敢以疾自便乎！」

translations.literal: He declined, saying, "In office one must bear one's responsibility—how dare I seek ease because of illness!"
translations.idiomatic: He declined, saying, "While I hold office I must bear its responsibilities. How dare I use illness as an excuse for comfort!"

sentences.zh: 於是疾益甚，還家而卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: Thereupon his illness grew worse; he returned home and died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: His illness then grew worse. He returned home and died at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 士大夫哭之皆失聲。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials wept for him until they lost their voices.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials wept for him until they could no longer speak.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾拊其柩曰：「世方嘉軟熟而惡崢嶸，求勁直如吾經父者，今無有矣！」

translations.literal: Su Shi beat upon his coffin and said, "The age just now praises the soft and ripe and loathes the rugged and towering; to seek someone as firm and straight as my Jingfu—there is none today!"
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi struck the coffin and said, "The age now praises the soft and pliable and hates the rugged and upright. To find someone as firm and straight as my Jingfu—there is no one left!"

sentences.zh: 詔厚恤其家，命弟平仲為江東轉運判官，視其葬。

translations.literal: An edict generously compensated his family and ordered his younger brother Pingzhong to serve as judicial intendant of the Jiangdong transport commission to oversee the burial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered generous compensation for his family and appointed his younger brother Pingzhong as judicial intendant on the Jiangdong transport commission to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 初，文仲與弟武仲、平仲皆以文聲起江西，時號「三孔」。

translations.literal: At first Wenzhong and his younger brothers Wuzhong and Pingzhong all rose to fame in Jiangxi through literary reputation; they were called the "Three Kongs."
translations.idiomatic: At first Wenzhong and his younger brothers Wuzhong and Pingzhong all rose to fame in Jiangxi through their literary reputations and were known as the "Three Kongs."

sentences.zh: 後追貶梅州別駕。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously demoted to Vice Prefect of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously demoted to Vice Prefect of Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 元符末，復其官。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanfu, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanfu era, his official rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 有文集五十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected works in fifty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in fifty volumes.

sentences.zh: 弟 武仲

translations.literal: Younger brother Wuzhong
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother: Wuzhong

sentences.zh: 武仲，字常父。

translations.literal: Wuzhong, style name Changfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhong, courtesy name Changfu.

sentences.zh: 幼力學，舉進士，中甲科。

translations.literal: From youth he studied hard, passed the jinshi examination, and placed in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied diligently, passed the jinshi examination, and ranked in the top grade.

sentences.zh: 調穀城主簿，選教授齊州，為國子直講。

translations.literal: He was assigned as clerk of Gucheng, selected as professor in Qizhou, and served as lecturer in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed clerk of Gucheng, selected as professor in Qizhou, and later served as lecturer in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 喪二親，毀瘠特甚，右肱為不舉。

translations.literal: When both parents died, his grief left him emaciated; his right arm became unable to lift.
translations.idiomatic: After both parents died, his grief left him severely emaciated, and he lost the use of his right arm.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，歷秘書省正字、校書，集賢校理，著作郎，國子司業。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, he served successively as proofreader in the Secretariat, collator, collator in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, Compiler, and Vice Director of Education in the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanyou era he served in succession as proofreader in the Secretariat, collator, collator in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, Compiler, and Vice Director of Education in the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 嘗論科舉之弊，詆王氏學，請復詩賦取士。

translations.literal: He once discussed the flaws of the examination system, decried the Wang school, and requested restoration of poetry-and-prose for selecting scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He once criticized the flaws of the examination system, condemned the Wang school, and called for restoring poetry-and-prose composition as a basis for selecting officials.

sentences.zh: 又欲罷大義，而益以諸經策，御試仍用三題。

translations.literal: He also wished to abolish the "Great Meaning" examination and add instead policy questions on the various classics; the palace examination would still use three topics.
translations.idiomatic: He also wanted to abolish the Great Meaning examination and replace it with policy questions on the various classics, while keeping three topics for the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 進起居郎兼侍講邇英殿，除起居舍人，數月，拜中書舍人，直學士院。

translations.literal: He advanced to Attendant Diarist and concurrent lecturer in the Hall of Lit Classics, was appointed Diarist, and within months was appointed Secretariat Drafter and academician on duty in the Hanlin Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Diarist and concurrent lecturer in the Hall of Lit Classics, appointed Diarist, and within a few months was made Secretariat Drafter and academician on duty in the Hanlin Institute.

sentences.zh: 初，罷侍從轉對，專責以論思。

translations.literal: At first the rotating court addresses by attendants were abolished, with sole responsibility placed on deliberative thought.
translations.idiomatic: At first the rotating court addresses by attendants had been abolished, leaving deliberative counsel as their sole duty.

sentences.zh: 武仲言：「苟不持之以法，則言與不言，將各從其意。

translations.literal: Wuzhong said, "If not maintained by rule, whether one speaks or not will each follow his own inclination.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhong said, "If this is not upheld by fixed rules, then whether one speaks or stays silent will depend entirely on personal whim.

sentences.zh: 願輪二人次對。」

translations.literal: I ask that two men be rotated to address the throne in turn."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that two men be rotated to address the throne in turn."

sentences.zh: 時議祠北郊，久不決。

translations.literal: At the time there was debate over sacrificing at the Northern Suburbs, long unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time debate over sacrificing at the Northern Suburbs had dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 武仲建用純陰之月親祠，如神州地祇。

translations.literal: Wuzhong proposed that in a purely yin month the emperor personally sacrifice, as with the Spirit Altar to the Earth Within the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhong proposed that the emperor personally perform the sacrifice in a purely yin month, following the precedent of the Spirit Altar to the Earth Within the Realm.

sentences.zh: 擢給事中，遷禮部侍郎，以寶文閣待制知洪州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Censor, moved to Vice Minister of Rites, with the added title of Academic Expectant of Baowen Pavilion and as prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Censor, transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, and appointed Academic Expectant of Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 請從臣為州者，杖以下公坐止劾官屬，俟獄成，聽大理約法，庶幾刑不逮貴近，又全朝廷體貌之意。

translations.literal: He requested that for court followers serving as prefect, for punishments below the staff, public trial should only impeach subordinate officials; wait until the case is complete, let the Court of Judicial Review apply the law—so punishment does not reach the nobles and near ones, while also preserving the court's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that when court officials served as prefects, in public trials for offenses punishable by caning or less, only their subordinates be impeached initially; once the case was complete, the Court of Judicial Review would apply the law. In this way punishment would not reach the high and the near, while the dignity of the court would still be preserved.

sentences.zh: 遂著為令。

translations.literal: This was then established as law.
translations.idiomatic: This was then written into law.

sentences.zh: 徙宣州，坐元祐黨奪職，居池州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Xuanzhou, demoted for Yuanyou faction affiliation, and lived in Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xuanzhou, stripped of office for affiliation with the Yuanyou faction, and lived in Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 元符末，追復之。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanfu, he was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanfu era, his rank was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 所著《詩書論語說》、《金華講義》、內外制、雜文共百餘卷。

translations.literal: He authored commentaries on the Poetry, Documents, and Analects, the Jinhua Lectures, inner and outer edicts, and miscellaneous writings totaling over a hundred volumes.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Expositions on the Poetry, Documents, and Analects, the Jinhua Lectures, inner and outer edicts, and miscellaneous essays, totaling more than a hundred volumes.

sentences.zh: 弟 平仲

translations.literal: Younger brother Pingzhong
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Pingzhong

sentences.zh: 平仲，字義甫。

translations.literal: Pingzhong, courtesy name Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong, whose courtesy name was Yifu,

sentences.zh: 登進士第，又應制科。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examinations and also took the special imperial decree examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations and also competed in the special imperial decree examination.

sentences.zh: 用呂公著薦，為秘書丞、集賢校理。

translations.literal: Through Lü Gongzhu's recommendation, he was made Secretary of the Palace Library and collating editor in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: On Lü Gongzhu's recommendation, he was appointed Secretary of the Palace Library and collating editor in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 文仲卒，歸葬南康。

translations.literal: Wenzhong died and was returned for burial at Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzhong died, his body was taken back to Nankang for burial.

sentences.zh: 詔以平仲為江東轉運判官護葬事，提點江浙鑄錢、京西刑獄。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Pingzhong as judicial intendant of the Jiangdong transport commission to oversee the burial, and as intendant over Jiangsu-Zhejiang coin casting and capital intendant of the Capital West circuit for criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Pingzhong as judicial intendant on the Jiangdong transport commission to supervise the funeral, while also assigning him oversight of coin minting in Jiangsu and Zhejiang and the criminal-judgment intendant post for the Capital West circuit.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，言者詆其元祐時附會當路，譏毀先烈，削校理，知衡州。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng period, memorialists attacked him for currying favor with those in power during the Yuanyou era and reviling former worthies; his collating editorship was stripped and he was made prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era, critics accused him of having sided with those in power during Yuanyou and of insulting former worthies. He was stripped of his collating editorship and made prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 提舉董必劾其不推行常平法，陷失官米之直六十萬，置獄潭州。

translations.literal: Commissioner Dong Bi impeached him for failing to implement the Ever-Normal Granary Law, alleging loss of official grain worth six hundred thousand, and placed him in prison at Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner Dong Bi charged him with failing to enforce the Ever-Normal Granary Law and with causing the loss of six hundred thousand in value of official grain; he was imprisoned at Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 平仲疏言：「米貯倉五年半，陳不堪食，若非乘民闕食，隨宜泄之，將成棄物矣。

translations.literal: Pingzhong memorialized: "The grain had been stored in granaries for five and a half years and had spoiled and was inedible; if it were not released as suited the people's food shortage, it would become waste.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong submitted a memorial: "The grain had lain in storehouses for five and a half years until it was stale and unfit to eat. Unless it was released when the people were short of food, as circumstances required, it would have become nothing but waste.

sentences.zh: 儻以為非，臣不敢逃罪。」

translations.literal: If this is deemed wrong, your subject dare not evade punishment."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty considers this wrong, I dare not shirk punishment."

sentences.zh: 乃徙韶州。

translations.literal: He was thereupon transferred to Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 又坐前上書之故，責惠州別駕，安置英州。

translations.literal: Again, because of having previously submitted a memorial, he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Huizhou and settled at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again punished for his earlier memorial, demoted to Vice Prefect of Huizhou, and assigned to live at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，復朝散大夫，召為戶部、金部郎中，出提舉永興路刑獄，帥鄜延、環慶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended, he was restored as Gentleman for Spread of Learning and summoned as bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and then in the Bureau of the Currency; he went out as commissioner over criminal cases in Yongxing circuit and commanded Yan-Yan and Huan-Qing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong came to the throne, Pingzhong was restored to Gentleman for Spread of Learning and summoned to serve as bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and then in the Bureau of the Currency. He was posted to supervise criminal cases in Yongxing circuit and given command over Yan-Yan and Huan-Qing.

sentences.zh: 黨論再起，罷，主管袞州景靈官，卒。

translations.literal: When factional disputes arose again, he was dismissed, placed in charge of the Jingling Shrine at Yanzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When factional strife broke out again, he was removed from office, put in charge of the Jingling Shrine at Yanzhou, and died there.

sentences.zh: 平仲長史學，工文詞，著《續世說》、《繹解稗》、《詩戲》諸書傳於世。

translations.literal: Pingzhong was deeply versed in historiography and skilled in literary composition; his works Continuation of Tales of the World, Interpretive Unravelings, Poetic Play, and others circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhong was deeply learned in history and a skilled writer. His Continuation of Tales of the World, Interpretive Unravelings, Poetic Play, and other works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 李周，字純之，馮翊人。

translations.literal: Li Zhou, courtesy name Chunzhi, was a native of Fuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhou, courtesy name Chunzhi, came from Fuyi.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，調長安尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examinations and was assigned as sheriff of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examinations, he was posted as sheriff of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，官為粥以食餓者，民坌集不可禁，縣以屬周，周設梐枑，間老少男女，無一亂者。

translations.literal: In a year of famine, the government provided gruel to feed the hungry; the people crowded together in a mass that could not be restrained. The county entrusted this to Zhou; Zhou set up barricades and separated old and young, men and women, and not a single disorder occurred.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year the government served congee to feed the hungry, but the people crowded together in numbers that could not be controlled. The county magistrate put Zhou in charge. Zhou set up barricades and sorted people by age and sex; not one instance of disorder occurred.

sentences.zh: 都巡檢趙瑜詰盜南山，諸尉皆屬焉，瑜悍急，多行無禮，獨於周不敢肆。

translations.literal: Chief circuit inspector Zhao Yu pursued bandits in South Mountain; all the sheriffs were subordinated to him. Yu was fierce and harsh and often behaved without propriety, but toward Zhou alone he dared not act wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: Chief circuit inspector Zhao Yu was hunting bandits on South Mountain, and all the local sheriffs were placed under his command. Yu was brutal and quick-tempered and often acted rudely, but he never dared behave that way toward Zhou.

sentences.zh: 轉洪洞令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Hongdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Hongdong.

sentences.zh: 民有世絕而官錄其產者，其族晚得遺券，周取以還之。

translations.literal: There were people whose line had died out and whose property the government had recorded; their clan later obtained a testamentary deed, and Zhou took it and returned it to them.
translations.idiomatic: When a family line died out and the government seized its property, the relatives later recovered a deed of inheritance. Zhou took it from the county records and returned it to them.

sentences.zh: 郡吏咎周，周曰：「利民，所以利國也。」

translations.literal: The prefectural clerks blamed Zhou. Zhou said: "Benefiting the people is how one benefits the state."
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural clerks reproached Zhou. He replied, "What benefits the people benefits the state."

sentences.zh: 縣之南有澗，支流湓入，歲賦菑楗，調徒遏之。

translations.literal: South of the county was a stream with branching tributaries surging in; each year a levy was assessed for flood control and corvée laborers were drafted to stem it.
translations.idiomatic: South of the county lay a gully whose tributaries surged in. Every year the county assessed a levy for flood works and drafted laborers to block the water.

sentences.zh: 周始築新堤，民不告病。

translations.literal: Zhou for the first time built a new dike, and the people made no complaint of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou built a new dike, and the people were no longer burdened.

sentences.zh: 改知雲安縣，蠲鹽井之征且百萬。

translations.literal: He was changed to be prefect of Yun'an County and remitted salt-well levies of nearly a million.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as prefect of Yun'an County, where he remitted nearly a million in salt-well taxes.

sentences.zh: 通判施州。

translations.literal: He served as vice-prefect of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice-prefect of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 州介群獠，不習服牛之利，為辟田數千畝，選謫戍知田者，市牛使耕，軍食賴以足。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered many Liao tribespeople who were unaccustomed to the advantage of using oxen; he opened several thousand mu of fields, selected exiled garrison men who knew farming, bought oxen to make them plow, and military provisions thereby came to suffice.
