translations.idiomatic: The prefecture bordered many tribal peoples who were unused to working with oxen. Li Zhou opened several thousand mu of farmland, selected exiled troops who knew how to farm, bought oxen for them to plow with, and thereby made the army's food supply sufficient.

sentences.zh: 司馬光將薦為御史，欲使來見，周曰：「司馬公之賢，吾固願見，但聞薦而往，所謂『呈身御史』也。」

translations.literal: Sima Guang was about to recommend him as censor and wanted him to come for an audience. Zhou said: "Sima Gong's worthiness—I indeed wish to meet him, but to go upon hearing of a recommendation is what is called 'presenting oneself for censorial appointment.'"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang was about to recommend him for the Censorate and wanted Zhou to pay him a visit first. Zhou said, "I would gladly meet Sima Gong, but to go see him once I have heard there is a recommendation would make me one of those 'censors who offer themselves up.'"

sentences.zh: 卒不往。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never went.

sentences.zh: 神宗詔近臣舉士，孫固以周聞。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong ordered close ministers to recommend scholars; Sun Gu brought Zhou to his attention.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong ordered his close advisers to recommend talented men, Sun Gu brought Li Zhou to the emperor's attention.

sentences.zh: 神宗召對，謂曰：「知卿不遊權門，識今執政乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong summoned him for audience and said: "Knowing that you do not haunt the gates of power, do you know the present chief ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhou for an audience and asked, "I know you never cultivate the powerful. Do you know the men in charge of the government today?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不識也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I do not know them."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I do not."

sentences.zh: 「識司馬光乎？」

translations.literal: Do you know Sima Guang?"
translations.idiomatic: And do you know Sima Guang?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「不識也。」

translations.literal: He said: "I do not know him."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I do not."

sentences.zh: 訪禦邊之術，曰：「四邊，手足爾。

translations.literal: He was asked about methods for defending the borders. He said: "The four frontiers are like the limbs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked him about defending the frontiers. Zhou said, "The four borders are like arms and legs.

sentences.zh: 若疲中國以勤遠略，致百姓窮困，聚為盜賊，懼成腹心之憂。」

translations.literal: If one exhausts the Central Plain to pursue distant campaigns and causes the common people to fall into destitution and gather as bandits, I fear one will bring about trouble at the very heart."
translations.idiomatic: If we wear down the heartland pursuing distant ambitions until the people are ruined and turn to banditry, we will face disaster at the very core of the empire."

sentences.zh: 神宗頷之，翼日，語固曰：「李周，樸忠之士也。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded; the next day he told Sun Gu: "Li Zhou is an honest and loyal man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded. The next day he told Sun Gu, "Li Zhou is a plain, loyal man.

sentences.zh: 朕且以為御史。」

translations.literal: I shall soon appoint him censor."
translations.idiomatic: I intend to make him a censor."

sentences.zh: 執政意其異己，請試以事。

translations.literal: The chief ministers took him to be unlike themselves and requested that he be tried out in office first.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers suspected he would not align with them and asked that he first be tested in an office before being made censor.

sentences.zh: 除提點京西刑獄。

translations.literal: He was appointed intendant of criminal cases in the Capital West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed criminal-judgment intendant for the Capital West circuit.

sentences.zh: 時方興水利，或請釃湍河為六渠，以益鉗廬陂水，度用工八十萬。

translations.literal: At the time water conservancy works were being promoted; some requested diverting the Tuan River into six canals to increase the water supply to Qianlu Lake, with an estimated labor cost of eight hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Waterworks were then being promoted throughout the empire. Some proposed diverting the Tuan River into six canals to boost the water held at Qianlu Lake, with an estimated cost of eight hundred thousand work units.

sentences.zh: 周曰：「湍河原高委下，捍以堤，猶患決溢，若又導之，必致為害。」

translations.literal: Zhou said: "The Tuan River rises high at its source and flows downward; even defended with dikes one still fears breach and overflow—if it is further channeled, harm will surely result."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou objected: "The Tuan River runs from high ground down a steep course. Even with dikes we still fear breaches and floods. If we add channels on top of that, we will surely cause disaster."

sentences.zh: 乃疏言：「渠成未可必，而費已不貲。

translations.literal: He then memorialized: "The canals' completion is not certain, yet the expense is already incalculable.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial: "There is no guarantee the canals will succeed, but the cost is already beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 盍姑鑿其一而試之，儻可以足用，行之。」

translations.literal: Why not first dig one and try it? If it proves sufficient in use, proceed."
translations.idiomatic: Why not dig just one canal first as a trial? If it proves adequate, then implement the rest."

sentences.zh: 渠卒無功。

translations.literal: In the end the canals accomplished nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The canals ultimately came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 明年，河溢，鄧城幾沒，始思其議。

translations.literal: The next year the river overflowed and Dengcheng nearly was submerged; only then did they reflect on his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the river flooded and nearly swallowed Dengcheng; only then did people reconsider his advice.

sentences.zh: 竟以直道罷，判西京國子監。

translations.literal: In the end, because of his upright path he was dismissed and made director of the Directorate of Education at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the end his uncompromising integrity cost him his post, and he was made director of the Directorate of Education at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 慈聖后復土，庀職陵下，中貴人至者旁午，次舍帟幕，競為華靡。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Cisheng's tomb was being completed, he was assigned duties at the mausoleum. Eunuchs arrived in swarms; their lodgings and tents vied in sumptuous display.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Cisheng's tomb was being completed, he was assigned duties at the burial site. Eunuchs arrived in endless succession, and their lodgings and canopies competed in lavish ornament.

sentences.zh: 周曰：「臣子執喪，不能寢苫枕塊，奈何又從而侈乎？」

translations.literal: Zhou said: "As subjects observing mourning, we cannot even sleep on straw and rest our heads on clods—how then can we follow them in extravagance?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said, "As mourners we cannot even properly sleep on straw and clods on the ground. How can we join them in extravagance?"

sentences.zh: 訖役，山陵使第功載，人人自言，周獨否。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, the imperial mausoleum commissioner ranked merits for the record; everyone spoke of his own, and Zhou alone refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the work ended, the imperial mausoleum commissioner ranked everyone's achievements for the record. Everyone claimed credit; Zhou alone declined.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，召為職方郎中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended, he was summoned as bureau director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong came to the throne, Li Zhou was recalled as bureau director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議和西夏，畀以侵地，至欲棄蘭州。

translations.literal: The court debated peace with Western Xia and ceding seized territory, even to the point of wishing to abandon Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated making peace with Western Xia by yielding seized territory, even to the point of abandoning Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 周曰：「隴右故為唃氏所有，常為吾藩籬。

translations.literal: Zhou said: "Longyou was formerly held by the Gu clan and has long served as our bulwark.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou argued, "Longyou once belonged to the Gu clan and has long served as our outer defense.

sentences.zh: 今唃氏破滅，若棄之，必歸夏人。

translations.literal: Now that the Gu clan is destroyed and extinguished, if we abandon it, it will surely revert to the Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Gu clan has been destroyed, if we abandon the region it will surely fall to the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 彼以區區河南，百年為敵，苟益以河湟，是盡得吐蕃之地，非秦、蜀之利也。」

translations.literal: They hold only the narrow lands south of the Yellow River and have been our enemies for a hundred years; if they gain the He-Huang region as well, they will come to hold all the Tibetan lands—this is not to the advantage of Qin and Shu."
translations.idiomatic: They hold only a strip south of the Yellow River and have been our enemies for a century. If we also hand them the He-Huang region, they will control all the Tibetan lands—and that will not benefit Qin and Shu."

sentences.zh: 遂不果棄。

translations.literal: In the end they did not abandon it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Lanzhou was not abandoned.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿、秘書少監，以直龍圖閣為陝西轉運使，復入為太常少卿，進權工部侍郎，旋以集賢院學士知邠州，恩禮如待制。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice Director of the Secretariat; as Hanlin associate at the Dragon Diagram Pavilion he served as Shaanxi transport commissioner; he was recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; advanced to Acting Vice Minister of Works; soon as Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies he was made prefect of Binzhou with honors like a drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice Director of the Secretariat, then served as Shaanxi transport commissioner with the rank of Hanlin associate at the Dragon Diagram Pavilion. Recalled to the capital as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he rose to Acting Vice Minister of Works and soon afterward was made prefect of Binzhou as Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, with honors like those of a drafting official.

sentences.zh: 徙鳳翔府、河中府、陝州，提舉崇福宮，改集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Fengxiang prefecture, Hezhong prefecture, and Shaanzhou; served as commissioner of Chongfu Palace; and was changed to collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred in turn to Fengxiang, Hezhong, and Shaanzhou, served as commissioner of Chongfu Palace, and was made collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，追貶賀州別駕，後復舊職。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng period he was posthumously demoted to Vice Prefect of Hezhou; later his original rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era he was posthumously demoted to Vice Prefect of Hezhou, but his former rank was later restored.

sentences.zh: 周自為小官，沉晦自匿，未嘗私謁執政，有公事，公詣中書白之。

translations.literal: From his days as a minor official, Zhou kept himself obscure and hidden; he never paid private visits to chief ministers—when there was official business, he would go openly to the Secretariat to report it.
translations.idiomatic: From his earliest days as a low official, Zhou kept himself withdrawn and obscure. He never paid private calls on those in power; when he had official business, he went openly to the Secretariat to report it.

sentences.zh: 薛向使三司，欲辟為屬，及相見，卒不敢言，退而歎曰：「若人未易屈也。」

translations.literal: Xue Xiang directed the Three Fiscal Departments and wished to recruit him as an aide; when they met, in the end he dared not speak of it, and upon departing sighed: "Such a man is not easily bent."
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Xiang directed the Three Fiscal Departments he wanted to recruit Zhou as an aide, but when they met he ultimately did not dare raise the subject. As he left he sighed, "A man like that is not easily bent."

sentences.zh: 以是不偶於世。

translations.literal: Because of this he did not find his match in the world.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason he never found his place in the world.

sentences.zh: 鮮于侁

translations.literal: Xian Yushen.
translations.idiomatic: The biography turns to Xian Yushen.

sentences.zh: 鮮于侁，字子駿，閬州人。

translations.literal: Xian Yushen, courtesy name Zijun, was a native of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xian Yushen, courtesy name Zijun, came from Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐劍南節度使叔明裔孫也。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Shuming, military governor of Jiannan in Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He was a descendant of Shuming, the Tang military governor of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 性莊重，力學。

translations.literal: By nature he was grave and solemn and devoted himself to learning.
translations.idiomatic: Grave and dignified by nature, he applied himself diligently to learning.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為江陵右司理參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examinations and served as judicial assistant in the right section at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examinations, he served as judicial assistant in the right section at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，天下旱，詔求言。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era drought spread across the realm, and an edict solicited opinions.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era a drought afflicted the empire, and the throne issued an edict calling for memorials.

sentences.zh: 侁推災變所由興，又條當世之失有四，其語剴切。

translations.literal: Yushen traced the origins by which disasters and anomalies arose and also listed four failings of the present age; his language was incisive.
translations.idiomatic: Yushen traced the causes of calamities and omens and set out four failings of the age in language that was sharp and forceful.

sentences.zh: 唐介與同鄉里，稱其名於上官，交章論薦。

translations.literal: Tang Jie was from the same home district; he praised Yushen's name to his superiors, and they jointly submitted memorials recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jie, a fellow townsman, praised him to his superiors, and together they submitted memorials recommending him.

sentences.zh: 侁盛言左參軍李景陽、枝江令高汝士之美，乞移與之，介益以為賢。

translations.literal: Yushen greatly praised the merits of Left Section Assistant Li Jingyang and Zhijiang Magistrate Gao Rushi and requested transfer to them; Jie considered him even more worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Yushen spoke at length of the virtues of Left Section Assistant Li Jingyang and Zhijiang Magistrate Gao Rushi and asked to be transferred so they could take his place; Jie thought him even more admirable for it.

sentences.zh: 調黟令，攝治婺源。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Yi and acted in the administration of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Yi and also handled the administration of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 奸民汪氏富而狠，橫里中，因事抵法，群吏羅拜曰：「汪族敗前令不少，今不舍，後當詒患。」

translations.literal: A wicked commoner of the Wang clan was rich but ruthless and domineered the community; when he was caught by the law, the clerks all bowed in a circle and said: "The Wang clan has ruined not a few previous magistrates; if you do not release him now, later you will bring disaster upon yourself."
translations.idiomatic: A local bully of the Wang clan was wealthy and ruthless and lorded it over the neighborhood. When he was caught breaking the law, the clerks all bowed before Yushen and said, "The Wangs have ruined many magistrates before you. If you do not let him go now, you will bring trouble on yourself later."

sentences.zh: 侁怒，立杖之，惡類屏跡。

translations.literal: Yushen grew angry, immediately had him beaten with the staff, and evil sorts vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: Yushen flew into a rage and had him caned on the spot; the local bullies disappeared from sight.

sentences.zh: 通判綿州。

translations.literal: He served as vice-prefect of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice-prefect of Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 綿處蜀左，吏狃貪成風，至課卒伍供薪炭、芻豆，鬻果蔬多取贏直。

translations.literal: Mian lay in the western part of Shu; officials were habituated to greed as a prevailing custom, even taxing soldiers to supply fuel and fodder and selling vegetables and fruit while taking excessive profit.
translations.idiomatic: Mian lay on the western edge of Shu, where officials had grown accustomed to greed. They even taxed the soldiers for fuel and fodder and sold vegetables and fruit at inflated prices.

sentences.zh: 侁一切弗取，郡守以下效之。

translations.literal: Yushen took none of it, and the prefect and those below followed his example.
translations.idiomatic: Yushen refused every such levy, and the prefect and all officials beneath him followed his lead.

sentences.zh: 趙抃使蜀，薦於朝，未及用。

translations.literal: Zhao Bian on a mission to Shu recommended him to the court, but he was not yet employed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Bian went on mission to Shu he recommended Yushen to the court, but the appointment had not yet been made.

sentences.zh: 從何郯辟，簽書永興軍判官。

translations.literal: Recruited by He Yan, he signed documents as vice-commander of the Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited by He Yan, he served as signing secretary to the vice-commander of the Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 萬年令不任職，繫囚累百，府使往治，數日，空其獄。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Wannian was incompetent in office; prisoners accumulated to over a hundred. The prefectural commissioner sent Yushen to handle it, and within days the jail was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Wannian was incompetent, and more than a hundred prisoners piled up in the jail. The prefect sent Yushen to take charge, and within days he had cleared the prison.

sentences.zh: 神宗詔求直言，侁為蔡河撥發，應詔陳十六事，神宗愛其文。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong ordered blunt speech sought; Yushen was a distribution clerk on the Cai River and responded to the edict with sixteen items; the emperor admired his writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong called for blunt memorials, Yushen, then serving as a distribution clerk on the Cai River, responded with sixteen proposals. The emperor admired his writing.

sentences.zh: 詔近臣舉所知，范鎮以侁應選，除利州路轉運判官。

translations.literal: An edict ordered close ministers to recommend men they knew; Fan Zhen nominated Yushen for selection, and he was appointed judicial intendant of the Lizhou transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered close ministers to recommend men they knew. Fan Zhen nominated Yushen, and he was appointed judicial intendant on the Lizhou transport commission.

sentences.zh: 初，王安石居金陵，有重名，士大夫期以為相。

translations.literal: At first Wang Anshi resided at Jinling with a great reputation, and scholar-officials expected that he would become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Wang Anshi was living at Jinling, he enjoyed enormous renown, and scholar-officials expected him to become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 侁惡其沽激要君，語人曰：「是人若用，必壞亂天下。」

translations.literal: Yushen loathed his ostentatious display to win the ruler and told people: "If this man is employed, he will surely ruin and disorder the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Yushen despised Wang's theatrical posturing to win the emperor's favor and told others, "If that man is put in power, he will surely throw the realm into chaos."

sentences.zh: 至是，乃上書論時政，曰：「可為憂患者一，可為太息者二，其他逆治體而召民怨者，不可概舉。」

translations.literal: At this point he submitted a memorial discussing current politics, saying: "There is one matter that may cause worry, two that may draw deep sighs, and other things that violate the governing order and summon popular resentment— these cannot all be enumerated."
translations.idiomatic: At this point he submitted a memorial on current affairs, saying, "There is one matter worth worrying over, two worth grieving over, and other policies that violate sound governance and stir popular resentment—too many to list in full."

sentences.zh: 其意專指安石。

translations.literal: His intent specifically targeted Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: His target was unmistakably Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 安石怒，毀短之。

translations.literal: Anshi grew angry and slandered him with disparagement.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was furious and spoke against him.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「侁有文學，可用。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said: "Yushen has literary talent and may be employed."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong said, "Yushen is a man of learning and can be used."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「陛下何以知之？」

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Your Majesty, how do you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi asked, "Your Majesty, how do you know that?"

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「有章奏在。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "There are memorials on record."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I have his memorials on file."

sentences.zh: 安石乃不敢言。

translations.literal: Anshi then dared not speak further.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi said no more.

sentences.zh: 初，助役法行，詔諸路各定所役緡錢。

translations.literal: At first, when the labor-exemption law was implemented, an edict ordered each circuit to fix the amount of cash to be levied for corvée substitution.
translations.idiomatic: When the labor-exemption law was first implemented, an edict ordered each circuit to set the cash levy for corvée substitution.

sentences.zh: 利州轉運使李瑜定四十萬，侁爭之曰：「利州民貧地瘠，半此可矣。」

translations.literal: Lizhou transport commissioner Li Yu fixed it at four hundred thousand; Yushen disputed it, saying: "The people of Lizhou are poor and the land is barren—half this amount would suffice."
translations.idiomatic: The Lizhou transport commissioner Li Yu set the levy at four hundred thousand. Yushen objected: "The people of Lizhou are poor and the land is barren. Half that amount would be enough."

sentences.zh: 瑜不從，各以其事聞。

translations.literal: Yu did not agree, and each reported the matter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu refused, and each man reported the dispute to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時諸路役書皆未就，神宗是侁議，諭司農曾布使頒以為式。

translations.literal: At the time the corvée registers of the various circuits were not yet complete; Emperor Shenzong approved Yushen's proposal and instructed Minister of Revenue Zeng Bu to promulgate it as a model.
translations.idiomatic: Since the corvée registers for the various circuits were not yet complete, the emperor sided with Yushen and instructed Zeng Bu, the Minister of Revenue, to promulgate his plan as the model.

sentences.zh: 因黜瑜，而升侁副使，仍兼提舉常平。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yu was dismissed, and Yushen was promoted to vice commissioner while still concurrently serving as commissioner of the Ever-Normal Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu was removed from office, and Yushen was promoted to vice commissioner while retaining his post as commissioner of the Ever-Normal Granary.

sentences.zh: 部民不請青苗錢，安石遣吏廉按，且詰侁不散之故。

translations.literal: The people in his circuit did not request Green Sprouts money; Anshi sent officials to investigate and also questioned Yushen as to why he did not distribute it.
translations.idiomatic: The people in his circuit did not apply for Green Sprouts loans. Wang Anshi sent officials to investigate and demanded to know why Yushen had not distributed the funds.

sentences.zh: 侁曰：「青苗之法，願取則與，民自不願，豈能強之哉！」

translations.literal: Yushen said: "Under the Green Sprouts law, those who wish to borrow receive loans—if the people themselves do not wish it, how can one force them!"
translations.idiomatic: Yushen replied, "Under the Green Sprouts law, loans are given to those who want them. If the people do not want them, how can we force them?"

sentences.zh: 左藏庫使周永懿守利州，貪虐不法，前使者畏其凶，莫敢問。

translations.literal: Left Treasury Storekeeper Zhou Yongyi guarded Lizhou, greedy and cruel and lawless; previous commissioners feared his ferocity and none dared investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yongyi, Left Treasury Storekeeper, was stationed at Lizhou. Greedy, brutal, and lawless, he had intimidated previous commissioners, and none had dared to investigate him.

sentences.zh: 侁捕械於獄，流之衡湘，因請更以文臣為守，並易班行領縣事。

translations.literal: Yushen arrested him and clapped him in fetters in prison, exiled him to Heng and Xiang, and thereupon requested that civil officials be substituted as prefects and that military officers in regular ranks be replaced to administer county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yushen had him arrested and thrown into prison in chains, then exiled him to the Heng and Xiang region. He also petitioned that civil officials replace military prefects and that county affairs no longer be entrusted to officers on the regular military roster.

sentences.zh: 凡居部九年，治所去閬中近，姻戚旁午，待之無所私，各得其歡心。

translations.literal: Altogether he remained in the circuit nine years; his seat of government was near Langzhong, and relatives and affines crisscrossed the region—yet he treated them without partiality, and each obtained his desired satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the circuit for nine years in all. His administrative seat lay close to Langzhong, his hometown, and relatives by blood and marriage were everywhere—but he showed them no favoritism, and everyone was content.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾稱侁上不害法，中不廢親，下不傷民，以為「三難」。

translations.literal: Su Shi praised Yushen, saying that above he did not harm the law, in the middle he did not abandon kin, and below he did not injure the people, and called this the "three difficulties."
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi praised Yushen for meeting what he called the "three difficulties": upholding the law without compromise, honoring kin without partiality, and governing the people without harm.

sentences.zh: 二稅輸絹綿，侁奏聽民以畸零納直。

translations.literal: For the two taxes paid in silk and cotton, Yushen memorialized that the people be allowed to pay cash for fractional amounts.
translations.idiomatic: When the two tax levies required payment in silk and cotton, Yushen petitioned to let people pay cash for odd fractional amounts instead.

sentences.zh: 其後有李元輔者，輒變而多取之，父老流涕曰：「老運使之法，何可改？」

translations.literal: Later there was one Li Yuanfu, who abruptly changed the practice and took more; the village elders wept and said: "The Old Transport Commissioner's law—how can it be altered?
translations.idiomatic: Later a man named Li Yuanfu changed the practice and extracted more from the people. The village elders wept and said, "The Old Transport Commissioner's policy—how can anyone change it?

sentences.zh: 蓋侁之侄師中亦居是職，故稱「老」以別之。

translations.literal: For Yushen's nephew Shizhong also held this post, so they called him "Old" to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: Yushen's nephew Shizhong had also held the same post, so the people called Yushen "Old" to tell the two men apart.

sentences.zh: 徙京東西路。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Jingdong and Jingxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to the Jingdong and Jingxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 河決澶淵，議欲勿塞，侁言：「東州彙澤惟兩濼，夏秋雨淫，猶溢而害，若縱大河注其中，民為魚矣。」

translations.literal: The Yellow River broke through at Chanyuan, and debate arose over not blocking it. Yushen said: "In the eastern provinces the gathering marshes are only the two Luo pools; in summer and autumn the rains are heavy, and even so they overflow and cause harm—if the great river is allowed to pour into them, the people will become fish."
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst its banks at Chanyuan, some officials argued against sealing the breach. Yushen said, "In the eastern provinces there are only two marshlands to receive floodwater. Even in ordinary summers and autumns, heavy rains make them overflow and cause damage. If we let the main river pour into them, the people will be drowned wholesale."

sentences.zh: 作《議河書》上之，神宗嘉納。

translations.literal: He composed the "Memorial on the River" and submitted it; Emperor Shenzong praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a "Memorial on the River" and submitted it to the throne, and Emperor Shenzong praised and adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 後兩路合為一，以侁為轉運使。

translations.literal: Later the two circuits were merged into one, and Yushen was made transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the two circuits were later merged into one, Yushen was appointed transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時王安石、呂惠卿當路，正人多不容。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Anshi and Lu Huiqing held the road of power, and upright men were for the most part not tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi and Lu Huiqing were then in power, and upright officials were largely shut out.

sentences.zh: 侁曰：「吾有薦舉之權，而所列非賢，恥也。」

translations.literal: Yushen said: "I have the power of recommendation, yet if those I list are not worthy men, it is shameful."
translations.idiomatic: Yushen said, "I have the power to recommend men for office. If I name the unworthy, that would be a disgrace."

sentences.zh: 故凡所薦如劉摯、李常、蘇軾、蘇轍、劉攽、范祖禹，皆守道背時之士。

translations.literal: Therefore all those he recommended, such as Liu Zhi, Li Chang, Su Shi, Su Zhe, Liu Ban, and Fan Zuyu, were men who upheld the Way against the times.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, everyone he recommended—Liu Zhi, Li Chang, Su Shi, Su Zhe, Liu Ban, Fan Zuyu, and others—were men who held to principle in defiance of the prevailing fashion.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年召對，命知揚州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng he was summoned for audience and ordered to serve as prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfeng he was summoned to audience and appointed prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「廣陵重鎮，久不得人，今朕自選卿往，宜善治之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said: "Guangling is a key stronghold and has long gone without the right man. Now I myself have chosen you to go— you should govern it well."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong told him, "Guangling is a vital stronghold that has long lacked the right man to govern it. I have chosen you myself for the post. See that you govern it well."

sentences.zh: 蘇軾自湖州赴獄，親朋皆絕交。

translations.literal: Su Shi, coming from Huzhou to face imprisonment, found that relatives and friends all severed ties with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi was being taken from Huzhou to prison, relatives and friends alike cut him off.

sentences.zh: 道揚，侁往見，臺吏不許通。

translations.literal: Passing through Yangzhou, Yushen went to see him, but the censorate clerks would not permit contact.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi passed through Yangzhou, Yushen went to visit him, but the censorate clerks refused to allow them to meet.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「公與軾相知久，其所往來書文，宜焚之勿留，不然，且獲罪。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "You and Shi have known each other long; the letters and writings exchanged between you ought to be burned and not kept—otherwise you will soon incur guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told him, "You and Su Shi have been friends for years. You should burn every letter and document you exchanged with him and leave nothing behind, or you will soon be implicated."

sentences.zh: 侁曰：「欺君負友，吾不忍為，以忠義分譴，則所願也。」

translations.literal: Yushen said: "To deceive the ruler and fail a friend— I cannot bear to do that; to receive punishment in accordance with loyalty and righteousness is what I wish."
translations.idiomatic: Yushen replied, "I cannot bring myself to deceive my sovereign or betray a friend. If I must suffer punishment for loyalty and righteousness, that is what I want."

sentences.zh: 為舉吏所累，罷主管西京御史臺。

translations.literal: He was implicated because of the clerks he had recommended and was dismissed from supervising the Western Capital Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the clerks he had recommended, he was implicated and removed from his post supervising the Western Capital Censorate.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，念東國困於役，吳居厚掊斂虐害，竄之，復以侁使京東。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended the throne, remembering that the eastern states were afflicted by corvée labor, he banished Wu Juho for exaction and cruel harm and again sent Yushen to govern Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong came to the throne, mindful that the eastern provinces were being crushed by corvée burdens, he banished Wu Juho for extortion and abuse and again dispatched Yushen to Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 司馬光言於朝曰：「以侁之賢，不宜使居外。

translations.literal: Sima Guang spoke in court, saying: "Given Yushen's worthiness, he ought not be kept in outer posts.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang told the court, "A man as worthy as Yushen should not be kept in provincial office.

sentences.zh: 顧齊魯之區，凋敝已甚，須侁往救之，安得如侁百輩，布列天下乎？」

translations.literal: Yet the Qi and Lu region is already grievously depleted and must have Yushen go to rescue it—how could one obtain a hundred men like Yushen and spread them across the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: But the Qi and Lu region is already badly depleted and needs Yushen to go save it. Where could we find a hundred men like him and post them across the empire?"

sentences.zh: 士民聞其重臨，如見慈父母。

translations.literal: When scholars and commoners heard that he was returning, it was as if they were seeing kind parents again.
translations.idiomatic: When scholars and commoners learned he was returning, they greeted him as though a loving parent had come home.

sentences.zh: 召為太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 侍從議神宗廟配享，有欲用王安石、吳充者，侁曰：「先朝宰相之賢，誰出富弼右？」

translations.literal: The attendant ministers debated who should receive paired sacrifice in Emperor Shenzong's temple; some wished to use Wang Anshi and Wu Chong. Yushen said: "Among the worthy chief ministers of the previous reign, who ranks above Fu Bi?
translations.idiomatic: When the attendant ministers debated who should share sacrifice in Emperor Shenzong's temple, some proposed Wang Anshi and Wu Chong. Yushen asked, "Among the previous reign's chief ministers, who was worthier than Fu Bi?

sentences.zh: 乃用弼。

translations.literal: Fu Bi was then used.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi was chosen instead.

sentences.zh: 拜左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as Left Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 侁見哲宗幼冲，首言君子小人消長之理甚備。

translations.literal: Yushen, seeing that Zhezong was young and tender in years, first spoke at length on the principle of the waxing and waning of gentlemen and petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Emperor Zhezong was still a child, Yushen began by setting out in full the principle of how gentlemen and petty men rise and fall in influence.

sentences.zh: 又言：「制舉，誠取士之要，國朝尤為得人。

translations.literal: He also said: "The decree examination is truly essential to selecting scholars, and our dynasty has especially excelled at obtaining men thereby.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The decree examination is truly central to selecting talent, and our dynasty has been especially successful at finding good men through it.

sentences.zh: 王安石用事，諱人詆訾新政，遂廢其科。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held power, he forbade people to slander the new policies and therefore abolished that examination category.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi was in power, he forbade criticism of the new policies and abolished the examination.

sentences.zh: 今方搜羅俊賢，廓通言路，宜復六科之舊。」

translations.literal: Now that outstanding worthies are being gathered and the path of speech is being opened wide, the old six categories ought to be restored."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the court is seeking out talented men and opening the channels of remonstrance, the old six examination categories should be restored."

sentences.zh: 又乞罷大理獄，許兩省、諫官相往來，減特奏名舉人，嚴出官之法，京東鹽得通商，復三路義勇以寬保甲，罷戎、瀘保甲以寬民力，事多施行。

translations.literal: He also begged to abolish the Dali prison, to allow the Two Departments and remonstrance officials to communicate with one another, to reduce specially nominated examinees, to tighten the law on leaving office, to allow free trade in Jingdong salt, to restore the three-circuit voluntary militia in order to relax the baojia system, and to abolish the baojia system in Rong and Lu to ease the people's burden—many of these measures were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to abolish the Dali prison; allow remonstrance officials and the Two Departments to communicate freely; reduce the number of specially nominated examinees; tighten rules on leaving office; permit free trade in Jingdong salt; restore the three-circuit voluntary militia to ease the baojia burden; and abolish baojia registration in Rong and Lu to spare the people. Many of these proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 在職三月，以疾求去。

translations.literal: After three months in office he requested leave on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After three months in office he asked to retire because of illness.

sentences.zh: 除集賢殿修撰、知陳州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and sent to govern Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔滿歲進待制。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that after one full year he be advanced to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promised that after one year he would be promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 居無何，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: Before long he died, at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he died, at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 侁刻意經術，著《詩傳》、《易斷》，為范鎮、孫甫推許。

translations.literal: Yushen devoted himself assiduously to classical learning and wrote commentaries on the Odes and the Changes; Fan Zhen and Sun Fu praised and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yushen devoted himself to classical learning and wrote commentaries on the Odes and the Changes, winning the praise of Fan Zhen and Sun Fu.

sentences.zh: 孫復與論《春秋》，謂今學者不能如之。

translations.literal: Sun Fu discussed the Spring and Autumn Annals with him and said that scholars of the present day could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Fu discussed the Spring and Autumn Annals with him, he declared that no scholar of the day could equal him.

sentences.zh: 作詩平澹淵粹，尤長於《楚辭》，蘇軾讀《九誦》，謂近屈原、宋玉，自以為不可及也。

translations.literal: The poetry he composed was plain, deep, and pure, and he was especially skilled in the Songs of Chu; Su Shi, reading his "Nine Chants," said it approached Qu Yuan and Song Yu, and considered himself unable to reach it.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was plain yet profound, and he was especially gifted in the Songs of Chu tradition. When Su Shi read his "Nine Chants," he said it rivaled Qu Yuan and Song Yu—and admitted he could not match it.

sentences.zh: 顧臨，字子敦，會稽人。

translations.literal: Gu Lin, courtesy name Zidun, was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Lin, courtesy name Zidun, came from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 通經學，長於訓詁。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics and excelled in exegetical glossing.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics and was especially skilled in textual exegesis.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，舉說書科，為國子監直講，遷館閣校勘、同知禮院。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era he passed the Lecturing Examination, served as Direct Lecturer in the Directorate of Education, and was promoted to collator in the Palace Library and Associate Director of the Court of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou era he passed the Lecturing Examination and became Direct Lecturer in the Directorate of Education, then rose to collator in the Palace Library and Associate Director of the Court of Rites.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，神宗以臨喜論兵，詔編《武經要略》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era, because the emperor was pleased that Lin enjoyed discussing military affairs, he ordered the compilation of the Essentials of Military Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining era, pleased that Gu Lin enjoyed discussing military affairs, Emperor Shenzong ordered the compilation of the Essentials of Military Classics.

sentences.zh: 初命都副承旨提舉，神宗謂臨館職，改提舉曰館幹。

translations.literal: At first the Deputy Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat was ordered to direct the project; the emperor, considering that Lin held a library post, changed the title from director to library steward.
translations.idiomatic: At first a deputy commissioner of the Palace Secretariat was appointed to direct the project, but since Gu Lin held a library post, the emperor changed the title from director to library steward.

sentences.zh: 且召臨問兵，對曰：「兵以仁義為本，動靜之機，安危所繫，不可輕也。」

translations.literal: The emperor also summoned Lin to question him on military affairs. He replied: "War takes benevolence and righteousness as its foundation; the pivot of action and inaction is bound up with safety and danger, and cannot be treated lightly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also summoned Gu Lin to question him about military affairs. He replied, "War must be grounded in benevolence and righteousness. The decision to act or hold back bears on the realm's safety and must never be taken lightly."

sentences.zh: 因條十事以獻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set forth ten items and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a list of ten recommendations.

sentences.zh: 出權湖南轉運判官，提舉常平。

translations.literal: He went out to serve concurrently as judicial intendant of the Hunan transport commission and as intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve concurrently as judicial intendant on the Hunan transport commission and as intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 議事戾執政意，罷歸。

translations.literal: Because his deliberations ran counter to the chief ministers' intent, he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When his policy views clashed with those of the chief ministers, he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 改同判武學，進集賢校理、開封府推官，請知潁州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Associate Administrator of the Military Academy, advanced to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and investigating officer in the Kaifeng prefectural office, and requested appointment as prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Associate Administrator of the Military Academy, promoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and investigating officer in the Kaifeng prefectural office, and then requested appointment as prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部郎中、秘書少監，以直龍圖閣為河東轉運使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, and with the rank of Direct Access to the Dragon Diagram Hall served as transport commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, then served as transport commissioner of Hedong with the rank of Direct Access to the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年，擢給事中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou he was promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanyou he rose to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方事回河，拜臨天章閣待制、河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: The court was then engaged in returning the Yellow River to its old course, and Lin was appointed Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and Chief Transport Commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was working to return the Yellow River to its old course, Gu Lin was appointed Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and Chief Transport Commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 於是，翰林學士蘇軾與李常、王古、鄧溫伯、孫覺、胡宗愈言：「臨資性方正，學有根本，慷慨中立，無所回撓。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hanlin Academician Su Shi, together with Li Chang, Wang Gu, Deng Wenbo, Sun Jue, and Hu Zongyu, said: "Lin's native endowment is upright and square, his learning has deep roots, he is magnanimous and stands in the middle, and he bends to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Su Shi, together with Li Chang, Wang Gu, Deng Wenbo, Sun Jue, and Hu Zongyu, wrote, "Gu Lin is upright by nature, grounded in solid learning, magnanimous and impartial, and incapable of being swayed.

sentences.zh: 自處東省，封駁論議，凜然有古人之風。

translations.literal: Since taking his place in the Eastern Secretariat, in sealing and rejecting and in debate he has been stern, with the air of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Since serving in the Eastern Secretariat, his memorials of approval and rejection have carried the stern authority of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 僥幸之流，側目畏憚。

translations.literal: The faction of opportunists look askance and fear him.
translations.idiomatic: Opportunists watch him with sidelong glances and dread him.

sentences.zh: 忽去朝廷，眾所嗟惜，宜留置左右，以補闕遺，別選深知河事者往使河北。」

translations.literal: Suddenly removed from court, he is lamented by all; he ought to be kept at the ruler's side to supply what is lacking, and another deeply versed in river affairs should be chosen to go to Hebei."
translations.idiomatic: His sudden removal from court is widely lamented. He should be kept close to the throne to remedy omissions in policy, and someone else deeply versed in river management should be sent to Hebei instead."

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫梁燾亦言：「都漕之職，在外豈無其人，在朝求如臨者，恐不易得。」

translations.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Liang Can also said: "For the post of chief transport commissioner, are there not men outside the court? Yet in court, to seek one like Lin— I fear he is not easily obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grandee Liang Can also wrote, "There may be others who could fill the chief transport commissioner's post in the provinces, but at court a man like Gu Lin would be hard to replace."

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None of these received reply.
translations.idiomatic: None of these petitions received a response.

sentences.zh: 臨至部，請因河勢回使東流。

translations.literal: When Lin reached his jurisdiction, he requested that the river's force be used to turn it back so it flowed east.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu Lin took up his post, he petitioned to use the river's current to restore its eastward flow.

sentences.zh: 復以給事中召還。

translations.literal: He was again summoned back as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to the capital as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 歷刑、兵、吏三部侍郎兼侍讀，為翰林學 士。

translations.literal: He passed through the vice ministerships of Punishments, War, and Personnel while also serving as Lecturer-in-Waiting, and became Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Vice Minister of Punishments, War, and Personnel while also Lecturer-in-Waiting, and was appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，以龍圖閣學士知定州，徙應天、河南府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng he served as Hanlin Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Dingzhou, then was transferred to the Yingtian and Henan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaosheng era he served as Hanlin Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Dingzhou, then was transferred to the Yingtian and Henan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 中人梁惟簡坐嘗事宣仁太后得罪，過洛，轉運使郭茂恂狥時宰意，劾臨與之宴集，奪職知歙州，又以附會黨人，斥饒州居住。

translations.literal: The eunuch Liang Weijian, having incurred guilt for once serving Empress Xuanren, passed through Luoyang; Transport Commissioner Guo Maoxun, currying the chief ministers' intent, impeached Lin for feasting with him, stripped him of office and made him prefect of Shezhou, and further, for associating with factional men, banished him to reside at Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liang Weijian, who had fallen from favor for having served Empress Xuanren, passed through Luoyang. Transport Commissioner Guo Maoxun, eager to please the chief ministers, impeached Gu Lin for dining with him, stripped him of rank and made him prefect of Shezhou, then banished him to Raozhou for associating with the faction.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，追復之。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended the throne, his offices were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong came to the throne, Gu Lin's offices were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 李之純

translations.literal: Li Zhichun.
translations.idiomatic: The biography turns to Li Zhichun.

sentences.zh: 李之純，字端伯，滄州無棣人。

translations.literal: Li Zhichun, courtesy name Duanbo, was a native of Wudi in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhichun, courtesy name Duanbo, came from Wudi in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，為度支判官、江西轉運副使。

translations.literal: During the Xining era he served as judicial intendant in the Revenue Section and as Vice Transport Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xining reforms he served as judicial intendant in the Revenue Section and as Vice Transport Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 御史周尹劾廣西提點刑獄許彥先受邕吏金，命之純往究其端，乃起於出婢之口。

translations.literal: Censor Zhou Yin impeached Xu Yanxian, Guangxi judicial intendant, for receiving gold from a Yong official and ordered Zhichun to go investigate its source; it turned out to have originated from the mouth of a dismissed maid.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhou Yin accused Xu Yanxian, Guangxi judicial intendant, of taking a bribe from a Yong official and ordered Li Zhichun to investigate. The charge turned out to have originated in gossip from a dismissed maid.

sentences.zh: 之純以為蕪俚之言，不治，彥先得免。

translations.literal: Zhichun considered it coarse and vulgar speech and did not pursue the case; Yanxian thereby obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhichun judged the accusation crude and unfounded and declined to pursue it, and Xu Yanxian was cleared.

sentences.zh: 徙成都路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner of the Chengdu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as transport commissioner of the Chengdu circuit.

sentences.zh: 成都歲發官米六千石，損直與民，言者謂惠民損上，詔下其議。

translations.literal: Each year Chengdu issued six thousand shi of official grain at reduced price to the people; critics said it benefited the people but harmed the state, and an edict ordered the matter submitted for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Chengdu sold six thousand shi of government grain to the people at a reduced price. Critics called this a benefit to the people at the state's expense, and the throne ordered the policy reviewed.

sentences.zh: 之純曰：「蜀郡人恃此為生百年，奈何一旦奪之。」

translations.literal: Zhichun said: "The people of the Shu commanderies have relied on this for their livelihood for a hundred years—how can it be snatched away in a single day?
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhichun said, "The people of Shu have depended on this for their livelihood for a century. How can we take it away overnight?

sentences.zh: 事遂已。

translations.literal: The matter thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 秩滿復留，凡數歲，始還朝。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was kept on again; altogether several years passed before he at last returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was kept on for several more years before he finally returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 神宗勞之曰：「遐方不欲數易大吏，使劍外安靖，年穀屢豐，以彰朝廷綏遠之意，汝知之乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong comforted him, saying: "In distant regions one does not wish frequently to change great officials; to keep the lands beyond the Sword Pass tranquil and the harvests repeatedly abundant, thereby displaying the court's intent to pacify the far reaches— do you understand this?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong praised him, saying, "In distant regions we prefer not to change senior officials too often. You kept the lands beyond the Sword Pass peaceful and the harvests abundant year after year, showing the court's intent to bring stability to the frontier. Do you understand why we kept you there?

sentences.zh: 以為右司郎中，轉太僕卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Section Director and then transferred to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Section Director and then promoted to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，加直龍圖閣、知滄州，召為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was given the rank of Direct Access to the Dragon Diagram Hall and appointed prefect of Cangzhou, then summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era he was granted the rank of Direct Access to the Dragon Diagram Hall and appointed prefect of Cangzhou, then recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 未至，改集賢殿修撰、河北都轉運使，進寶文閣待制、知瀛州。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was changed to Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Chief Transport Commissioner of Hebei, advanced to Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Precious Culture, and made prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached the capital he was reassigned as Compiler at the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Chief Transport Commissioner of Hebei, promoted to Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Precious Culture, and appointed prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄以直學士知成都府，還為戶部，三遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, as Hanlin Academician he served as prefect of Chengdu; returning, he again became Minister of Revenue and was thrice promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as prefect of Chengdu as Hanlin Academician, then returned to the Ministry of Revenue and rose through three promotions to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 建言：「朝廷事下六部，但隨省吏視其前後批，以制緩急之序，是為胥吏顓處命令也。

translations.literal: He submitted a proposal: "When court affairs are sent down to the Six Ministries, they simply follow the clerks of each ministry in looking at the prior and subsequent endorsements to determine the order of urgency— this is to let petty clerks monopolize command.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "When court business reaches the Six Ministries, officials simply follow their clerks' reading of prior endorsements to decide what is urgent. That lets petty clerks control imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 若大臣不暇省，宜令列曹長貳隨其所承，當行即行，當止即止，必稟而後決，毋拘於文，則吏不得舞權，而下情達矣。」

translations.literal: If great ministers have no time to examine matters, the chief and deputy of each bureau should be ordered to act according to what they receive— when action is due, act; when it should stop, stop— and decisions need not always await formal report; do not be bound by paperwork, then clerks cannot manipulate power and lower sentiments will reach the top."
translations.idiomatic: If senior ministers lack time to review every document, the chiefs and deputies of each bureau should act on what they receive—proceed when action is required, halt when it is not—without waiting for endless formal approvals. If they are not bound by paperwork, clerks cannot manipulate power and grievances from below will reach the top."

sentences.zh: 又言：「眾賢和於朝，則萬物和於野。

translations.literal: He also said: "When many worthies are in harmony at court, then the myriad things are in harmony in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "When worthy men are united at court, harmony prevails throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 燮理陰陽，輔相之職。

translations.literal: Harmonizing yin and yang is the duty of the chief counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonizing yin and yang is the chief counselor's duty.

sentences.zh: 間者，國論稍虧雍睦，語言播傳，動係觀望，不可以不謹。」

translations.literal: Recently state discourse has slightly fallen short in cordial harmony; words spread abroad and movements are tied to watchful waiting— this must be treated with care."
translations.idiomatic: Lately court politics has grown less cordial. Rumors circulate and officials hesitate and watch one another. This demands careful attention."

sentences.zh: 董敦逸、黃慶基論蘇軾託詞命以毀先帝，蘇轍以名器私所親，皆以臨司罷，之純疏其誣罔，乃更黜之。

translations.literal: Dong Dunyi and Huang Qingji argued that Su Shi, under cover of edicts and orders, slandered the late emperor, and that Su Zhe used honors and offices to favor his intimates; both were dismissed by the censorate, but Zhichun memorialized that they had slandered falsely, and those men were instead demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Dunyi and Huang Qingji accused Su Shi of using imperial edicts to slander the late emperor and Su Zhe of bestowing honors on his favorites. Both accusers were dismissed by the censorate, but Li Zhichun petitioned that their charges were false, and the accusers were demoted instead.

sentences.zh: 以疾，改工部尚書。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he was changed to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he was reassigned as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，劉拯劾其阿附轍，出知單州。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng, Liu Zheng impeached him for currying favor with Su Zhe, and he was sent out as prefect of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era Liu Zheng impeached him for currying favor with Su Zhe, and he was sent out as prefect of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 從弟之儀。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin was Li Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 從弟 之儀

translations.literal: Younger cousin Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhiyi, a younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 之儀，字端叔。

translations.literal: Zhiyi, courtesy name Duanshu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhiyi, courtesy name Duanshu.

sentences.zh: 登第幾三十年，乃從蘇軾於定州幕府。

translations.literal: Nearly thirty years after passing the examination, he only then followed Su Shi in the staff of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly thirty years after passing the examinations, he finally joined Su Shi's staff at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷樞密院編修官，通判原州。

translations.literal: He passed through Compiler in the Bureau of Military Affairs and served as Vice Prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as compiler in the Bureau of Military Affairs and as Vice Prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 元符中，監內香藥庫。

translations.literal: During the Yuanfu era he supervised the Inner Spice and Medicine Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanfu era he was put in charge of the Inner Spice and Medicine Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 御史石豫言其嘗從蘇軾辟，不可以任京官，詔勒停。

translations.literal: Censor Shi Yu said that he had once followed Su Shi's summons and could not be entrusted with a capital office; an edict ordered his service suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shi Yu argued that because Li Zhiyi had once served under Su Shi's summons, he was unfit for a capital post. An edict ordered his appointment suspended.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初，提舉河東常平。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huizong's reign he was intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Huizong's reign he served as intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 坐為范純仁遺表，作行狀，編管太平，遂居姑熟，久之，徙唐州，終朝請大夫。

translations.literal: He was punished for writing the final memorial and funeral biography for Fan Chunren, was placed under registered banishment at Taiping, then dwelt at Gushu; after a long time he was moved to Tangzhou, and ended as Chaoxing Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for drafting Fan Chunren's deathbed memorial and funeral biography, was placed under registered banishment at Taiping, and settled at Gushu. Long afterward he was transferred to Tangzhou and ended his career as Chaoxing Grandee.

sentences.zh: 之儀能為文，尤工尺牘，軾謂入刀筆三昧。

translations.literal: Zhiyi could compose prose and was especially skilled at formal letters; Shi said he had entered the samadhi of the writing brush.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhiyi could write well and was especially masterful at formal correspondence; Su Shi said he had attained perfect mastery of the writer's art.

sentences.zh: 王覿，字明叟，泰州如皋人。

translations.literal: Wang Di, courtesy name Mingsou, was a man of Rugao in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Di, courtesy name Mingsou, was a native of Rugao in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，為編修三司令式刪定官。

translations.literal: During the Xining era he served as compilation and revision officer for the regulations of the three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era he served as an officer charged with compiling and revising the regulations of the three bureaus.

sentences.zh: 不樂久居職，求潤州推官。

translations.literal: Unhappy to remain long in office, he requested the post of judicial commissioner in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to linger long in a capital post, he asked to be made judicial commissioner in Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 二浙旱，郡遣吏視苗傷，承監司風旨，不敢多除稅。

translations.literal: The two Zhe regions suffered drought. Prefectures sent officials to inspect crop damage; following the circuit intendant's implicit intent, they dared not grant much tax relief.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck the two Zhe circuits, prefectures sent officials to inspect crop damage, but taking their cue from the circuit intendant, they dared not grant substantial tax relief.

sentences.zh: 覿受檄覆按，歎曰：「旱勢如是，民食已絕，倒廩贍之，猶懼不克濟，尚可責以賦邪？」

translations.literal: Di received orders to reinvestigate and sighed, saying, "The drought is this severe, the people's food is already exhausted. Even if we empty the granaries to sustain them, we still fear we cannot save them—how can we still demand taxes from them?"
translations.idiomatic: Di received orders to reinvestigate the reports and sighed, "The drought is this severe and the people already have nothing to eat. Even if we emptied the granaries to feed them, we would still fear we could not save them—how can we still demand taxes?"

sentences.zh: 行數日，盡除之。

translations.literal: After traveling several days, he exempted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: After several days on the road, he exempted the taxes entirely.

sentences.zh: 監司怒，捃摭百出。

translations.literal: The circuit intendant was enraged and collected faults from every direction.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit intendant was furious and dredged up fault after fault against him.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷遣使振貸，覿請見，為言民間利病。

translations.literal: It happened that the court sent envoys with relief grain and loans. Di requested an audience and spoke of the people's benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent envoys with relief grain and loans, Di asked to see them and laid out the people's hardships and needs.

sentences.zh: 使者喜，歸薦之，除司農寺主簿，轉為丞。

translations.literal: The envoy was pleased, recommended him on his return, and Di was appointed registrar of the Ministry of Revenue and later promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was pleased and recommended him on his return. Di was appointed registrar of the Ministry of Revenue and later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 司農時為要官，進用者多由此選。

translations.literal: At that time the Ministry of Revenue was a key office, and many who were advanced came through this route.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue was then a post of great importance, and many men on the fast track to advancement passed through it.

sentences.zh: 覿拜命一日，即求外，韓絳高其節，留檢詳三司會計。

translations.literal: One day after receiving the appointment, Di at once sought an outside posting. Han Jiang admired his integrity and kept him to examine and review the three bureaus' accounts.
translations.idiomatic: The day after accepting the appointment, Di asked to leave the capital for a provincial post. Han Jiang admired his integrity and kept him on to examine and review the accounts of the three bureaus.

sentences.zh: 絳出潁昌，辟簽書判官。

translations.literal: When Jiang went out to Yingchang, he recruited Di as secretary and judicial assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang was posted to Yingchang, he recruited Di as his secretary and judicial assistant.

sentences.zh: 坐在潤公闕免，屏居累年，起為太僕丞，徙太常。

translations.literal: Because of a fault while serving at Runzhou, he was dismissed from office, lived in seclusion for years, was then raised to vice director of the Imperial Stud, and transferred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a fault while serving at Runzhou, he was dismissed and lived in retirement for years. He was later recalled as vice director of the Imperial Stud and then transferred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，呂公著、范純仁薦其可大任，擢右正言，進司諫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Lü Gongzhu and Fan Chunren recommended him as fit for heavy responsibility. He was promoted to Right Rectifier and advanced to director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong came to the throne, Lü Gongzhu and Fan Chunren recommended him for high office. He was promoted to Right Rectifier and then to director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「國家安危治亂，係於大臣。

translations.literal: He memorialized the throne, saying, "The state's security, peril, order, and disorder depend on the grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "Whether the state stands secure or in peril, in order or in chaos, depends on its grand ministers.

sentences.zh: 今執政八人，而奸邪居半，使一二元老，何以行其志哉？」

translations.literal: Today there are eight men in the executive, yet half are treacherous and base. How can one or two senior worthies carry out their intent?"
translations.idiomatic: There are eight men in power today, yet half of them are treacherous and corrupt. With only one or two senior worthies among them, how can they carry out their aims?"

sentences.zh: 因極論蔡確、章惇、韓縝、張璪朋邪害正。

translations.literal: He then thoroughly argued that Cai Que, Zhang Dun, Han Zong, and Zhang Cao formed factions of the wicked and harmed the upright.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out at length how Cai Que, Zhang Dun, Han Zong, and Zhang Cao had banded together in wicked factions and harmed upright men.

sentences.zh: 章數十上，相繼斥去。

translations.literal: He submitted dozens of memorials, and they were dismissed from office one after another.
translations.idiomatic: He sent up dozens of memorials, and the men he named were driven from office one after another.

sentences.zh: 又劾竄呂惠卿。

translations.literal: He also impeached Lü Huiqing and had him banished.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Lü Huiqing and had him banished.

sentences.zh: 朝論以大奸既黜，慮人情不安，將下詔慰釋之，且戒止言者。

translations.literal: Court opinion held that since the great traitors had already been removed, it feared public sentiment would be unsettled and planned to issue an edict of consolation and release, and also to warn memorialists to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held that with the great villains already removed, public feeling might be unsettled. The court planned to issue a soothing edict and also to warn memorialists to hold their tongues.

sentences.zh: 覿言：「誠出於此，恐海內有識之士，得以輕議朝廷。

translations.literal: Di said, "If this truly comes from that concern, I fear men of insight throughout the realm will be able to look lightly upon the court.
translations.idiomatic: Di said, "If this truly proceeds from that concern, I fear that thoughtful men throughout the realm will come to hold the court in contempt.

sentences.zh: 舜罪四凶而天下服，孔子誅少正卯而魯國治。

translations.literal: When Shun punished the Four Villains, the realm submitted; when Confucius executed Shaozheng Mao, the state of Lu was well governed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun punished the Four Villains, the realm submitted; when Confucius executed Shaozheng Mao, the state of Lu was well governed.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，不聞人情不安，亦不聞 命令以悅其黨也。

translations.literal: At that time one did not hear that public sentiment was unsettled, nor did one hear of commands issued to please their faction.
translations.idiomatic: In those cases one never heard that the people were unsettled, nor that edicts were issued to placate the wrongdoers' allies.

sentences.zh: 蓋人君之所以御下者，黜陟二柄而已。

translations.literal: In general, what a ruler uses to control subordinates is simply the two handles of dismissal and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler controls his subordinates by two handles alone: dismissal and advancement.

sentences.zh: 陟一善而天下之為善者勸，黜一惡而天下之為惡者懼。

translations.literal: Advance one good man and all who do good throughout the realm are encouraged; dismiss one evil man and all who do evil are afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Advance one good man and all who would do good are encouraged; dismiss one wicked man and all who would do evil are afraid.

sentences.zh: 豈以為惡者懼而朝廷亦為之懼哉？

translations.literal: Would the court itself also be afraid because evildoers are afraid?
translations.idiomatic: Surely the court need not share the fear of those who have done evil?

sentences.zh: 誠為陛下惜之。」

translations.literal: I truly regret this on Your Majesty's behalf."
translations.idiomatic: I truly regret this on Your Majesty's behalf.

sentences.zh: 覿言雖切，然不能止也。

translations.literal: Though Di's words were forceful, he could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Di's words were forceful, but they could not stop the edict.

sentences.zh: 夏主新立，有輕中國心。

translations.literal: The Xia ruler had newly ascended the throne and had a mind to look down upon China.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia ruler had newly come to power and showed signs of contempt for the Song.

sentences.zh: 覿曰：「小羌窺我厭兵，故桀驁若是。

translations.literal: Di said, "These small Qiang tribes spy on our weariness of war, therefore they are so arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Di said, "These petty Qiang tribes see that we are weary of war, and that is why they act so arrogantly.

sentences.zh: 然所當憂者，不在今秋而在異日，所當謹者，不在邊備而在廟謨。

translations.literal: Yet what should worry us is not this autumn but days to come; what should be guarded is not border defenses but court strategy.
translations.idiomatic: What we should worry about is not this autumn but the days ahead; what we should guard is not the border alone but the strategy of the court.

sentences.zh: 翕張取予之權，必持重而後可。」

translations.literal: The power to contract and expand, take and give, must be held with weight before it can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: The power to tighten and loosen, to take and to give, must be exercised with restraint before it can succeed.

sentences.zh: 洮東擒鬼章，檻至闕下，覿曰：「老羌雖就擒，其子統眾如故，疆土種落未減於前，安可遽戮以賈怨。

translations.literal: Guizhang was captured east of the Tao River and sent in a cage to the palace. Di said, "Though the old Qiang chieftain has been captured, his son still commands the masses as before, and the border lands and tribal settlements are no fewer than before. How can we hastily execute him and invite resentment?
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhang was captured east of the Tao River and sent to the capital in a cage, Di said, "Though the old Qiang leader is taken, his son still commands the tribes as before, and our border lands and tribal settlements are no smaller than they were. How can we rush to execute him and invite fresh hatred?

sentences.zh: 宜處之洮、岷、秦、 雍間，以示含容好生之德，離其石交而壞其死黨。」

translations.literal: It would be better to place him among the Tao, Min, Qin, and Yong regions to show tolerant and life-loving virtue, split his rock-hard alliances, and ruin his die-hard faction."
translations.idiomatic: Better to place him among the Tao, Min, Qin, and Yong circuits, showing a tolerant and life-sparing policy, splitting his rock-solid alliances and breaking up his die-hard clique.

sentences.zh: 又言：「今民力凋瘵，邊費亡極，不可不深為之計。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Now the people's strength is exhausted, and border expenses are boundless. This must be planned for deeply."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The people's strength is now exhausted and border costs know no limit. We must plan for this with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 於是疏將帥非其人者請易之，茶鹽之害民者請革之，至逋債、振瞻、賦斂、科須，皆指陳其故。

translations.literal: Thereupon in his memorial he asked to replace unfit generals, reform tea and salt policies that harmed the people, and concerning arrears, relief, levies, and corvée requisitions, he pointed out the causes of each.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he asked that unfit commanders be replaced, that harmful tea and salt policies be reformed, and he set out the causes of trouble in arrears, relief, taxation, and corvée levies.

sentences.zh: 差役法復行，覿以為：「朝廷意在便民，而議者遂謂免役法無一事可用。

translations.literal: When the corvée-service law was restored, Di held that "the court's intent is to benefit the people, yet debaters then said the exemption-from-corvée law had not one usable provision.
translations.idiomatic: When the corvée-service law was restored, Di argued, "The court means to benefit the people, yet critics now say the exemption-from-corvée law had not a single provision worth keeping.

sentences.zh: 夫法無新舊，惟善之從。」

translations.literal: Laws are not about old or new—only follow what is good."
translations.idiomatic: Laws are not a matter of old versus new; one should follow whatever is good.

sentences.zh: 因采掇數十事於差法有助可以通行者上之。

translations.literal: He therefore gathered several dozen matters from the corvée law that could help implementation and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered several dozen provisions from the corvée law that could usefully be retained and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遂論青苗之害，乞盡罷新令，而復常平舊法，曰：「聚斂之臣，惟知罔利自媒，不顧後害。

translations.literal: He then discussed the harm of the Green Sprouts policy, begged to abolish all the new orders and restore the Ever-Normal old law, and said, "Men who gather wealth know only to seek profit and recommend themselves, heedless of later harm.
translations.idiomatic: He then argued the harm of the Green Sprouts policy and asked that all the new orders be abolished and the old Ever-Normal Granary law restored, saying, "Men who squeeze revenue know only how to chase profit and advance themselves, heedless of the harm that follows.

sentences.zh: 以國家之尊，而與民爭錐刀之利，何以示天下？」

translations.literal: With the state's dignity, to contend with the people for pinpricks of profit—how can this be shown to the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: When the state itself contends with the people over pennies, what lesson does that teach the realm?

sentences.zh: 又言：「刑罰世輕世重。

translations.literal: He also said, "Punishments are light or heavy according to the age.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Punishments are lighter or heavier according to the times.

sentences.zh: 熙寧大臣，謂刑罰不重，則人無所憚。

translations.literal: The Xining grand ministers held that if punishments were not heavy, people would have nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: The Xining grand ministers held that unless punishments were severe, people would have nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 今法令已行，可以適輕之時，願擇質厚通練之士，載加芟正。」

translations.literal: Now the statutes have been in force; this is a time when they may appropriately be lightened. I beg that solid, experienced men be selected to compile further revisions."
translations.idiomatic: The statutes have now been in force long enough that this is the time to lighten them. I ask that men of solid character and practical experience be chosen to revise them further.

sentences.zh: 於是置局編彙，俾覿預焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon a bureau was established for compilation, and Di was made to participate.
translations.idiomatic: A bureau was therefore established to compile the revisions, and Di was appointed to it.

sentences.zh: 大抵皆用中典，《元祐敕》是也。

translations.literal: For the most part they used the median statutes; such were the Yuanyou Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part they adopted the median standard of punishment—the Yuanyou Statutes were the result.

sentences.zh: 神宗復唐制，諫官分列兩省。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong restored the Tang system, with remonstrance officials divided between the two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong restored the Tang system, with remonstrance officials assigned to the two provinces.

sentences.zh: 至是，大臣議徙之外門，而以其直舍為制敕院，名防漏泄，實不欲使與給舍相通。

translations.literal: At this time the grand ministers proposed moving them outside the gate and using their quarters for the Edict Drafting Bureau—nominally to prevent leaks, but in fact not wanting them to communicate with the drafting and edict officers.
translations.idiomatic: Now the grand ministers proposed moving them outside the palace gate and turning their offices into the Edict Drafting Bureau—nominally to prevent leaks, but in truth to keep them from communicating with the drafting and edict officers.

sentences.zh: 覿爭之曰：「制敕院，吏舍也。

translations.literal: Di contested this, saying, "The Edict Drafting Bureau is clerks' quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Di objected, saying, "The Edict Drafting Bureau is a clerks' office.

sentences.zh: 奪諫省以廣吏舍，信胥吏而疑諍臣，何示不廣也。」

translations.literal: Seize the Remonstrance Bureau to expand clerks' quarters—trust petty clerks yet suspect remonstrating ministers. What lack of magnanimity does this show?"
translations.idiomatic: To seize the Remonstrance Bureau and enlarge a clerks' office—to trust petty clerks while distrusting remonstrating ministers—what narrowness of spirit does that reveal?

sentences.zh: 乃不果徙。

translations.literal: The move was therefore not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The move was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 覿在言路，欲深破朋黨之說。

translations.literal: While on the remonstrance path, Di wished deeply to break the talk of factions.
translations.idiomatic: While serving on the remonstrance path, Di was determined to break the power of faction talk.

sentences.zh: 朱光庭訐蘇軾試館職策問，呂陶辯其不然，遂起洛、蜀二黨之說。

translations.literal: Zhu Guangting impeached Su Shi over an Academy examination question; Lü Tao argued that this was not so, and thus arose talk of the Luo and Shu factions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guangting attacked Su Shi over an examination question for Academy posts; Lü Tao defended him, and from this arose talk of the Luo and Shu factions.

sentences.zh: 覿言：「軾之辭，不過失輕重之體爾。

translations.literal: Di said, "Shi's wording was merely a lapse in balancing severity—nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Di said, "Su Shi's wording was merely a lapse in calibrating severity—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 若悉考同異，深究嫌疑，則兩岐遂分，黨論滋熾。

translations.literal: If we examine every difference and probe every suspicion, the two branches will split and faction talk will grow fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: If every difference is investigated and every suspicion pursued to the end, the two camps will split apart and faction talk will burn hotter.

sentences.zh: 夫學士命詞失指，其事尚小；

translations.literal: When an academician's drafted edict misses the mark, the matter is still small;
translations.idiomatic: When an academician's drafted edict misses the mark, the matter is still small;

sentences.zh: 使士大夫有朋黨之名，大患也。」

translations.literal: to give scholars and officials the name of faction—that is the great disaster."
translations.idiomatic: but to give scholars and officials the brand of faction—that is the great disaster.

sentences.zh: 帝深然之，置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply agreed and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 尋改右司員外郎，未幾，拜侍御史、右諫議大夫。
