translations.literal: Soon he was changed to vice director in the Right Department; before long he was appointed investigating censor and Right Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director in the Right Department, and not long afterward was appointed investigating censor and Right Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 坐論尚書右丞胡宗愈，出知潤州，加直龍圖閣、知蘇州。

translations.literal: Punished for criticizing Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Hu Zongyu, he went out as prefect of Runzhou, was given the added title of Direct Academician of the Dragon Hall Pavilion, and served as prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for criticizing Vice Director Hu Zongyu of the Ministry of Personnel, he was sent out as prefect of Runzhou, given the added title of Direct Academician of the Dragon Hall Pavilion, and appointed prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 州有狡吏，善刺守將意以撓權，前守用是得譏議。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a cunning clerk skilled at probing the prefect's intent to undermine his authority; previous prefects had been criticized because of this.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had a cunning clerk who was adept at reading the prefect's mind and undermining his authority; earlier prefects had been criticized on his account.

sentences.zh: 覿窮其奸狀，置於法，一郡肅然。

translations.literal: Di thoroughly exposed his wrongdoing and punished him by law; the whole commandery became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Di thoroughly exposed the man's crimes and punished him according to law, and the whole commandery fell into order.

sentences.zh: 民歌詠其政，有「吏行水上，人在鏡心」之語。

translations.literal: The people sang of his governance, with the words, "Officials walk upon water; the people live in a mirror heart."
translations.idiomatic: The people sang praises of his rule, saying, "Officials walk upon water; the people dwell in a mirror-clear heart."

sentences.zh: 徙江淮發運使，入拜刑、戶二部侍郎，與豐稷偕使遼，為遼人禮重。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner for the Huai and Yangzi region, entered court as vice minister of Justice and of Revenue, and jointly served as envoy to Liao with Feng Ji, being honored by the Liao people.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner for the Huai and Yangzi region, then entered court as vice minister of Justice and of Revenue. He served jointly with Feng Ji as envoy to Liao and was treated with great respect by the Khitans.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，以寶文閣直學士知成都府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era he served as Direct Academician of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaosheng era he served as Direct Academician of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 蜀地膏腴，畝千金，無閑田以葬，覿索侵耕官地，表為墓田。

translations.literal: Shu land was fertile, worth a thousand cash per mu, and there was no idle land for burial. Di sought out encroachments on official land and memorialized that they be set aside as grave fields.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was rich land, worth a thousand cash per mu, with no spare ground for burial. Di tracked down encroachments on official land and memorialized that they be set aside as grave fields.

sentences.zh: 江水貫城中為渠，歲久湮塞，積苦霖潦而多水災，覿疏治復故，民德之，號「王公渠」。

translations.literal: River water ran through the city as a canal; after long years it silted up, and the people suffered endlessly from torrential rains and frequent floods. Di dredged and restored it, and the people thanked him, calling it Lord Wang's Canal.
translations.idiomatic: A channel cut from the river ran through the city, but after years of silt it was blocked, and the people suffered flood after flood. Di dredged it and restored it to its former course. The people were grateful and called it Lord Wang's Canal.

sentences.zh: 徙河陽，貶少府少監，分司南京，又貶鼎州團練副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Heyang, demoted to vice director of the Palace Workshops with a nominal post in Nanjing, and again demoted to vice commissioner of military training in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Heyang, then demoted to vice director of the Palace Workshops with a nominal post in Nanjing, and demoted again to vice commissioner of military training in Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，還故職，知永興軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, Di was restored to his former rank and made military commissioner of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong came to the throne, Di was restored to his former rank and appointed military commissioner of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 過闕，留為工部侍郎，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Passing through the capital, he was retained as vice minister of Works and promoted to censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed through the capital on his way to his post, he was kept on as vice minister of Works and then promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 改元詔下，覿言：「『建中』之名，雖取『皇極』。

translations.literal: When the edict changing the reign title was issued, Di said, "The name 'Jianzhong,' though taken from 'supreme norm,
translations.idiomatic: When the edict changing the reign title was issued, Di said, "The name Jianzhong, though drawn from the phrase 'supreme norm,

sentences.zh: 然重襲前代紀號，非是，宜以德宗為戒。」

translations.literal: yet repeats a former dynasty's reign title. This is wrong; one ought to take Emperor Dezong as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: repeats a reign title from a former dynasty. That is a mistake, and Emperor Dezong's example should serve as a warning.'

sentences.zh: 時任事者多乖異不同，覿言：「堯、舜、禹相授一道，堯不去四凶而舜去之，堯不舉元凱而舜舉之，事未必盡同；

translations.literal: At that time those in charge mostly diverged from one another. Di said, "Yao, Shun, and Yu transmitted one Way to one another. Yao did not remove the Four Villains, yet Shun removed them; Yao did not raise Yuan and Kai, yet Shun raised them—matters need not all be identical;
translations.idiomatic: At the time those in power were sharply at odds with one another. Di said, "Yao, Shun, and Yu handed down a single Way, yet Yao did not remove the Four Villains while Shun did; Yao did not raise Yuan and Kai while Shun did. Affairs need not be identical in every detail;

sentences.zh: 文王作邑於豐而武王治鎬，文王關市不征，澤梁無禁，周公征而禁之，不害其為善繼、善述。

translations.literal: King Wen made his capital at Feng while King Wu governed at Hao; Wen did not tax the markets and did not forbid marshes and weirs, yet the Duke of Zhou taxed and forbade them. This did not harm their being good successors and good continuers.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen built his capital at Feng while King Wu ruled from Hao; Wen levied no market taxes and placed no restrictions on marshes and weirs, yet the Duke of Zhou taxed and restricted them. That did not keep them from being worthy successors who carried on a worthy legacy.

sentences.zh: 神宗作法於前，子孫當守於後。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong established laws in front; descendants should guard them behind.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong established the laws; his descendants ought to uphold them.

sentences.zh: 至於時異事殊，須損益者損益之，於理固未為有失也。」

translations.literal: When times differ and affairs change, what must be reduced or increased should be reduced or increased—there is nothing lost in principle."
translations.idiomatic: When times change and circumstances differ, what must be trimmed or expanded should be trimmed or expanded. That is not, in principle, a failure of fidelity.

sentences.zh: 當國者忿其言，遂改為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Those holding power resented his words and thereupon changed his post to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power resented his words and transferred him to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 日食四月朔，帝下詔責躬，覿當制，有「惟德弗類，未足以當天心」之語，宰相去之，乃力請外。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month there was a solar eclipse. The emperor issued an edict blaming himself. Di was to draft it and included the words, "My virtue alone is not of the right kind and is not sufficient to answer Heaven's heart." The chief minister removed them, and Di then forcefully requested an outside posting.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month there was a solar eclipse, and the emperor issued a self-reproach edict. Di was assigned to draft it and wrote, "My virtue is not worthy, and I am not equal to Heaven's intent." The chief minister struck out the passage, and Di then pressed hard for a provincial appointment.

sentences.zh: 以龍圖閣學士知潤州，徙海州，罷主管太平觀，遂安置臨江軍。

translations.literal: He was made academician of the Dragon Hall Pavilion and prefect of Runzhou, transferred to Haizhou, dismissed from supervising the Taiping Observatory, and then settled at Linjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Dragon Hall Pavilion and prefect of Runzhou, then transferred to Haizhou, stripped of his charge over the Taiping Observatory, and finally placed under restricted residence at Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 覿清修簡澹，人莫見其喜慍。

translations.literal: Di was pure, restrained, simple, and detached; no one ever saw him pleased or angry.
translations.idiomatic: Di lived plainly and with restraint; no one ever saw him show pleasure or anger.

sentences.zh: 持正論始終，再罹譴逐，不少變。

translations.literal: He held to upright views from start to finish, suffered punishment and banishment twice, and did not change in the least.
translations.idiomatic: He held to upright views throughout, was punished and banished twice, and never wavered.

sentences.zh: 無疾而卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: He died without illness at the age of sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died without illness at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，追復龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: Early in the Shaoxing era his rank as academician of the Dragon Hall Pavilion was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing era his title of academician of the Dragon Hall Pavilion was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 從子俊義。

translations.literal: His nephew's son was Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew's son was Junyi.

sentences.zh: 從子 俊義

translations.literal: Nephew's son: Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew's son: Junyi

sentences.zh: 俊義，字堯明。

translations.literal: Junyi, courtesy name Yaoming.
translations.idiomatic: Junyi, courtesy name Yaoming.

sentences.zh: 遊學京師，資用乏，或薦之童貫，欲厚聘之，拒不答。

translations.literal: He studied in the capital, but his funds ran short. Someone recommended him to Tong Guan, who wished to hire him generously, but he refused to reply.
translations.idiomatic: While studying in the capital he ran short of money. Someone recommended him to Tong Guan, who wanted to hire him at a generous salary, but he refused even to answer.

sentences.zh: 林靈素設講席寶籙宮，詔兩學選士問道。

translations.literal: Lin Lingsu set up a lecture hall at the Baolu Palace, and an edict ordered scholars selected from both academies to inquire about the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Lingsu established a lecture hall at the Baolu Palace, and an edict ordered scholars chosen from both imperial academies to attend and inquire about the Way.

sentences.zh: 車駕將臨視推恩，司成以俊義及曹偉應詔，俊義辭焉。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage was about to visit and grant favor. The director of education nominated Junyi and Cao Wei in response to the edict, but Junyi declined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to visit in person and grant favors. The director of the Imperial College nominated Junyi and Cao Wei to answer the edict, but Junyi declined.

sentences.zh: 人曰：「此顯仕捷逕也，不可失。」

translations.literal: People said, "This is a shortcut to prominent office—you cannot miss it."
translations.idiomatic: People told him, "This is a fast track to high office—you must not let it slip by.

sentences.zh: 俊義曰：「使辭不獲命，至彼亦不拜。

translations.literal: Junyi said, "Even if my refusal is not accepted and I must go, when I arrive I still will not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Junyi replied, "Even if my refusal is overruled and I am forced to go, when I arrive I still will not bow.

sentences.zh: 倘見困辱，則以死繼之。」

translations.literal: If I should suffer humiliation, I will follow with death."
translations.idiomatic: If I am put to shame there, I will follow with my life.

sentences.zh: 逮至講所，去御幄跬步，內侍呼姓名至再，俊義但望幄致敬，不肯出；

translations.literal: When they reached the lecture hall, a few steps from the imperial screen, the inner attendant called his name twice, but Junyi only bowed toward the screen and refused to come forward;
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the lecture hall, only a few paces from the imperial screen, an inner attendant called his name twice. Junyi bowed toward the screen but refused to step forward;

sentences.zh: 次呼曹偉，偉回首，俊義目之，亦不出。

translations.literal: next Cao Wei was called; Wei looked back, and Junyi signaled with his eyes, and he too did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei was called next. Wei looked back, Junyi caught his eye, and he too stayed where he was.

sentences.zh: 既罷，皆為之懼，俊義處之恬然。

translations.literal: When it was over, all were afraid for him, but Junyi was perfectly calm.
translations.idiomatic: When it was over, everyone feared for him, but Junyi remained perfectly calm.

sentences.zh: 以太學上舍選，奏名列其下，徽宗親程其文，擢為第一。

translations.literal: Selected from the upper division of the Imperial Academy, his memorial ranked below others, but Huizong personally graded his essay and raised him to first place.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen from the upper division of the Imperial Academy, his submitted essay was initially ranked below others, but Huizong personally graded his paper and placed him first.

sentences.zh: 及賜第，望見容貌甚偉，大說，顧侍臣曰：「此朕所親擢也，真所謂『俊義』矣。

translations.literal: When the degree was granted, seeing that his appearance was very imposing, the emperor was greatly pleased and turned to his attendants, saying, "This is the man I personally selected—truly what is called 'handsome and righteous.
translations.idiomatic: When the degree was conferred, the emperor saw how imposing he looked and was greatly pleased. He turned to his attendants and said, "This is the man I personally chose—truly worthy of the name Junyi, 'handsome and righteous.

sentences.zh: 自古未有人主自為主司者，宜即超用。」

translations.literal: Since antiquity no sovereign has ever himself served as chief examiner; he should at once be exceptionally promoted."
translations.idiomatic: Never before has a ruler himself served as chief examiner. He should be promoted at once to high office."

sentences.zh: 蔡京邀使來見，曰：「一見我，左右史可立得。」

translations.literal: Cai Jing invited the messenger to have him come and see him, saying, "One meeting with me, and the posts of Left and Right Historian can be obtained at once."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing sent word inviting him to an audience and said, "Come see me once, and you can have the Left and Right Historian posts immediately."

sentences.zh: 俊義不往，僅拜國子博士。

translations.literal: Junyi did not go. He received appointment only as Lecturer at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Junyi refused to go. He accepted appointment only as a lecturer at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 居二年，乃得改太學博士。

translations.literal: After two years in office, he was finally transferred to Lecturer at the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was finally promoted to lecturer at the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 鄆王謁先聖，有司議諸生門迎。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan came to pay homage to the Sage, the responsible officials debated having the students greet him at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan came to visit the temple of the Sage, the officials in charge proposed that the students greet him at the gate.

sentences.zh: 俊義曰：「此豈可施於人臣哉？

translations.literal: Junyi said, "How can this ceremony be applied to a subject?
translations.idiomatic: Junyi said, "How can a ceremony like this be shown to a mere subject?

sentences.zh: 禮如見宰相足矣。」

translations.literal: The rites used when meeting the chief minister are quite sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: The etiquette appropriate to receiving a chief minister is quite enough."

sentences.zh: 乃序立敦化堂下，及王至，猶辭不敢當。

translations.literal: Thereupon they lined up in order below Dunhua Hall, and when the prince arrived, he still declined, not daring to accept the honor.
translations.idiomatic: So they formed ranks below Dunhua Hall, and when the prince arrived Junyi still demurred, saying he did not deserve such treatment.

sentences.zh: 進吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嘗入對，帝問：「卿知前所以親擢乎？

translations.literal: Once, on entering audience, the emperor asked, "Do you know why I personally selected and promoted you before?
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion, when he came before the emperor in audience, the emperor asked, "Do you know why I personally chose and promoted you?

sentences.zh: 蓋主司之意不一，是以天子自提文衡也。

translations.literal: It was because the chief examiners' judgments were not uniform, and so the Son of Heaven himself held the literary scales.
translations.idiomatic: The chief examiners could not agree, so the Son of Heaven himself held the scales of literary judgment.

sentences.zh: 衛膚敏、吳安國今安在？」

translations.literal: Where are Wei Fumin and Wu Anguo now?"
translations.idiomatic: Where are Wei Fumin and Wu Anguo now?"

sentences.zh: 具以對，即召為館職，而遷俊義右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He answered in full detail, whereupon Wei Fumin and Wu Anguo were at once summoned to archive posts, and Junyi was transferred to Assistant Secretary in the Right Division.
translations.idiomatic: He answered in full. Wei Fumin and Wu Anguo were immediately summoned to posts in the archives, and Junyi was transferred to assistant secretary in the Right Division.

sentences.zh: 為王黼所惡，以直秘閣知岳州。

translations.literal: Hated by Wang Fu, he was made Associate of the Secretariat Directly Attached and sent out as prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu took a dislike to him, and he was given the title of associate of the Secretariat and sent out to serve as prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 俊義與李祁友善，首建正論於宣和間。

translations.literal: Junyi was on friendly terms with Li Qi and was the first to establish orthodox discourse during the Xuanhe period.
translations.idiomatic: Junyi was close to Li Qi, and together they were the first to raise an orthodox voice during the Xuanhe reign.

sentences.zh: 當是時，諸公卿稍知分別善惡邪正，兩人力也。

translations.literal: At that time, the various grandees and ministers gradually came to distinguish good from evil and the orthodox from the heterodox—the two men's merit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the high officials gradually learned again to distinguish good from evil and the orthodox from the heterodox, and the credit belonged to these two men.

sentences.zh: 祁，字肅遠，亦知名士，官不顯。

translations.literal: Qi, courtesy name Suyuan, was also a well-known scholar, but his official career was not distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi, courtesy name Suyuan, was likewise a well-known scholar, though he never rose to prominent office.

sentences.zh: 馬默，字處厚，單州成武人。

translations.literal: Ma Mo, courtesy name Chuhou, was a man of Chengwu in Dan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Mo, courtesy name Chuhou, was a native of Chengwu in Dan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 家貧，徒步詣徂徠從石介學。

translations.literal: His family was poor. He went on foot to Mount Culai to study under Shi Jie.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and he walked all the way to Mount Culai to study under Shi Jie.

sentences.zh: 諸生時以百數，一旦出其上。

translations.literal: The students at the time numbered in the hundreds, yet in a single day he rose above them all.
translations.idiomatic: The students numbered in the hundreds, yet in no time he surpassed them all.

sentences.zh: 既而將歸，介語諸生曰：「馬君他日必為名臣，宜送之山下。」

translations.literal: When he was about to return home, Jie told the students, "Master Ma will surely become a famous minister one day. You ought to see him off at the foot of the mountain."
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to leave, Shi Jie told the students, "Master Ma will become a famous minister one day. You should see him off at the foot of the mountain."

sentences.zh: 登進士第，調臨濮尉，知須城縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as magistrate of Linpu, and served as prefect of Xucheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Linpu, and then served as prefect of Xucheng County.

sentences.zh: 縣為鄆治所，鄆吏犯法不可捕，默趨府，取而杖之客次，闔府皆驚。

translations.literal: The county was the seat of Yan Prefecture. Yan officials who broke the law could not be arrested, so Mo hurried to the prefectural seat, seized them, and beat them at the guest lodge. The whole prefecture was astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The county was the seat of Yan Prefecture, and Yan officials who broke the law could not ordinarily be arrested. Mo rushed to the prefectural seat, seized them, and had them beaten in the guest lodge. The whole prefecture was stunned.

sentences.zh: 曹佾守鄆，心不善也，默亦不為屈。

translations.literal: Cao Yi was prefect of Yan and took an unfavorable view of him, yet Mo would not yield either.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi, the prefect of Yan, took a dislike to him, but Mo would not bend.

sentences.zh: 後守張方平素貴，掾屬來前，多閉目不與語。

translations.literal: Later, when Zhang Fangping became prefect, he was by nature lofty in rank. When his staff came forward, he often closed his eyes and would not speak with them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhang Fangping became prefect, he was a man of high standing by nature. When his staff came before him, he often closed his eyes and refused to speak with them.

sentences.zh: 見默白事，忽開目熟視久之，盡行其言，自是諉以事。

translations.literal: When he saw Mo report business, he suddenly opened his eyes and stared at him intently for a long time, then fully carried out what Mo said. From then on he entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo came to report business, Zhang suddenly opened his eyes and studied him intently for a long while, then adopted everything Mo proposed. From then on he entrusted affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 治平中，方平還翰林，薦為監察御史裏行，遇事輒言無顧。

translations.literal: During the Zhiping period, when Fangping returned to the Hanlin Academy, he recommended Mo as Supervisory Censor in probationary status. On every matter that arose, Mo spoke out without regard for consequences.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping era, when Zhang Fangping returned to the Hanlin Academy, he recommended Mo as a probationary supervisory censor. On every issue that arose, Mo spoke out without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 方平間遣所親儆之曰：「言太直，得無累舉者乎？」

translations.literal: Fangping occasionally sent a close associate to warn him, saying, "Your words are too blunt—will this not harm the man who recommended you?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fangping occasionally sent a close associate to warn him, saying, "You speak too bluntly. Won't that bring trouble on the man who recommended you?"

sentences.zh: 默謝曰：「辱知之深，不敢為身謀，所以報也。」

translations.literal: Mo thanked him and said, "I am deeply honored by your knowing me well. I dare not scheme for my own sake—that is how I repay you."
translations.idiomatic: Mo replied with thanks, "You have honored me with your deep trust. I dare not look out for myself—that is how I repay you."

sentences.zh: 時議尊崇濮安懿王，臺諫呂誨等力爭以為不可，悉出補外。

translations.literal: At the time the court debated honoring Prince Pu the Respectful and Virtuous. The remonstrators and censors Lü Hui and others argued forcefully that this could not be done, and all were sent out to fill external posts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court debated elevating Prince Pu the Respectful and Virtuous. The remonstrators and censors, led by Lü Hui, argued forcefully that this could not be done, and all were sent out to provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 默請還之，不報。

translations.literal: Mo requested that they be restored [to court]. There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Mo petitioned that they be recalled to court, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 遂上言：「濮王生育聖躬，人誰不知。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial stating, "Prince Pu bore the sacred person—who does not know this?
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial saying, "Everyone knows that Prince Pu was the emperor's biological father.

sentences.zh: 若稱之為親，義無可據，名之不正，失莫大焉。

translations.literal: If he is styled as kin, there is no basis in right principle. When the name is not correct, the loss is beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: But if he is formally styled as imperial kin, there is no proper basis for it. When the name is wrong, the harm is incalculable.

sentences.zh: 願發自宸心，明詔寢罷，以感召和氣，安七廟之神靈，是一舉而眾善隨之也。」

translations.literal: I pray that this may issue from the imperial heart: let a clear edict halt and abandon the plan, so as to summon harmonious qi, settle the spirits of the seven ancestral temples, and achieve in one act the following of many goods."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will act from your own heart and issue a clear edict to abandon the plan, thereby drawing down harmonious qi and securing the spirits in the ancestral temples. One such act would bring many blessings in its train."

sentences.zh: 又言：「致治之要，求賢為本。

translations.literal: He also said, "The essential point of bringing about good governance is to seek the worthy as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "The key to good government is to seek out worthy men.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以官人之權，盡委輔相，數十年間，賢而公者無幾。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong delegated the power of appointing officials entirely to his chief ministers. Over several decades, there were few who were both worthy and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong had entrusted the power of appointment entirely to his chief ministers. Over several decades, few men of both talent and integrity rose to office.

sentences.zh: 官之進也，不由實績，不自實聲，但趨權門，必得顯仕。

translations.literal: Advancement in office did not come through real achievement or genuine reputation. One had only to court the doors of power to obtain a prominent post.
translations.idiomatic: Advancement did not depend on real achievement or genuine reputation. Those who flocked to the powerful invariably won prominent posts.

sentences.zh: 今待制以上，數倍祖宗之時，至謀一帥臣，則協於公議者十無三四。

translations.literal: Today those at the rank of dazhi and above are several times more numerous than in the time of the ancestors. Yet when a single field commander is to be chosen, only three or four in ten accord with public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at the rank of dazhi and above now outnumber those of the founders' era several times over, yet when the court chooses a single field commander, only three or four candidates in ten command broad agreement.

sentences.zh: 庶僚之眾，不知幾人，一有難事，則曰無人可使。

translations.literal: The multitude of ordinary officials—who knows how many there are? Yet whenever a difficult task arises, they say there is no one who can be sent.
translations.idiomatic: The ranks of officials are beyond counting, yet whenever a difficult task arises the court says there is no one fit to send.

sentences.zh: 豈非不才者在上，而賢不肖混淆乎？

translations.literal: Is this not because the unworthy are above, while the worthy and unworthy are confused together?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not because the unworthy hold the upper ranks while the capable and the incompetent are indistinguishable?

sentences.zh: 願陛下明目達聰，務既其實，歷試而超升之，以幸天下。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will open your eyes and sharpen your hearing, strive to verify reality, test men repeatedly and promote them exceptionally, and thereby bless all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will see clearly and listen keenly, judge men by their real merit, test them in office and promote the proven, and so bring blessing to the realm."

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中張師顏提舉諸司庫務，繩治不法，眾吏懼搖，飛語讒去之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shiyan, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice, was charged with supervising the treasury offices of the various departments. He disciplined illegal conduct, and the many clerks, fearing upheaval, spread slanderous rumors to have him removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shiyan of the Ministry of Justice was put in charge of supervising the treasury offices of the various departments. He cracked down on abuses, and the clerks, fearing for themselves, spread rumors to have him removed.

sentences.zh: 默力陳其故，以為：「惡直醜正，實繁有徒。

translations.literal: Mo forcefully set forth the reason, stating, "Those who hate the straight and revile the upright are indeed many.
translations.idiomatic: Mo forcefully explained the situation, writing, "Those who hate the upright and revile the righteous are indeed many.

sentences.zh: 今將去積年之弊，以興太平，必先官舉其職。

translations.literal: Now, if we are to remove abuses accumulated over many years and raise up great peace, we must first have officials perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: If we are to remove abuses accumulated over many years and restore great peace, officials must first be made to do their jobs.

sentences.zh: 宜崇獎師顏，厲以忠勤，則尸素括囊之徒，知所勸矣。」

translations.literal: Shiyan should be honored and rewarded and encouraged with loyalty and diligence. Then the crowd of deadwood purse-closers will know what to strive for."
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan should be honored and encouraged with loyalty and diligence. Then the idle officials who draw salaries and do nothing will know what is expected of them."

sentences.zh: 西京會聖宮將創仁宗神御殿，默言：「事不師古，前典所戒。

translations.literal: At Huisheng Palace in the Western Capital, a spirit hall for Emperor Renzong was about to be built. Mo said, "Affairs that do not take antiquity as model are what former canons warn against.
translations.idiomatic: At Huisheng Palace in the Western Capital, a spirit hall for Emperor Renzong was about to be built. Mo wrote, "To depart from ancient precedent is exactly what the classics warn against.

sentences.zh: 漢以諸帝所幸郡國立廟，知禮者非之。

translations.literal: Under the Han, shrines were established in the commanderies and kingdoms favored by the various emperors, and those who understood ritual criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, shrines were erected in the commanderies and kingdoms favored by successive emperors, and men who understood ritual condemned the practice.

sentences.zh: 況先帝未嘗幸洛，而創建廟祀，實乖典則。

translations.literal: Moreover, the late emperor never visited Luoyang, yet a shrine is to be newly built for his worship—this truly departs from canonical norms.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the late emperor never visited Luoyang, yet a shrine is to be built there for his worship. This truly violates canonical practice.

sentences.zh: 願以禮為之節，義為之制，亟止此役，以章清靜奉先之意。」

translations.literal: I pray that ritual may be used to restrain it and righteousness to regulate it, that this project be urgently halted, and thereby make manifest the intent of quiet reverence toward the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that ritual may set its bounds and righteousness govern it, and that this project be stopped at once, so as to show the spirit of quiet reverence toward the ancestors."

sentences.zh: 會地震河東、陝西郡，默以為陰盛，慮為邊患，宜備之。

translations.literal: At the same time, earthquakes struck the prefectures of Hedong and Shaanxi. Mo took this as a sign of excessive yin and, fearing border trouble, said preparations should be made.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time, earthquakes struck the prefectures of Hedong and Shaanxi. Mo took this as a sign of excessive yin and, fearing trouble on the frontier, urged that defenses be readied.

sentences.zh: 後數月，西夏果來侵。

translations.literal: Several months later, Western Xia indeed came to invade.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later, Western Xia did invade.

sentences.zh: 除知登州。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 沙門島囚眾，官給糧者才三百人，每益數，則投諸海。

translations.literal: On Shamen Island the prisoners were numerous. The grain supplied by the state fed only three hundred persons. Whenever the number increased, the excess were thrown into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: On Shamen Island the prisoners were many, but the state ration fed only three hundred. Whenever the number rose above that, the surplus were cast into the sea.

sentences.zh: 砦主李慶以二年殺七百人，默責之曰：「人命至重，恩既貸其生，又從而殺之，不若即時死鄉里也。

translations.literal: The fort commander Li Qing, over two years, killed seven hundred men. Mo rebuked him, saying, "Human life is of the utmost weight. Grace has already spared their lives, yet you then go on to kill them—this is worse than letting them die at once in their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: The fort commander Li Qing had killed seven hundred men over two years. Mo rebuked him, saying, "Human life is precious beyond measure. The state has already spared these men, yet you go on killing them. That is worse than letting them die at once in their home districts.

sentences.zh: 汝胡不以乏糧告，而顓殺之如此？」

translations.literal: Why did you not report the shortage of grain, but instead deliberately killed them like this?"
translations.idiomatic: Why did you not report the shortage of grain instead of slaughtering them on your own authority?"

sentences.zh: 欲按其罪，慶懼，自縊死。

translations.literal: He intended to investigate and punish him for the crime. Qing, in fear, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to investigate and punish Li Qing for the crime. Qing, terrified, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 默為奏請，更定《配島法》凡二十條，溢數而年深無過者移登州，自是多全活者。

translations.literal: Mo submitted a memorial requesting a revision of the Regulations for Exile to the Islands, twenty articles in all. Those above the quota who had been long on the island without offense were transferred to Dengzhou. From then on many more lives were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Mo memorialized the throne requesting a revision of the Regulations for Exile to the Islands, twenty articles in all. Prisoners above the quota who had been long on the island without offense were to be transferred to Dengzhou. From then on many more lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 其後蘇軾知登州，父老迎於路曰：「公為政愛民，得如馬使君乎？」

translations.literal: Later, when Su Shi became prefect of Dengzhou, the elders welcomed him on the road, saying, "Will you govern with love for the people as Prefect Ma did?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Su Shi became prefect of Dengzhou, the elders greeted him on the road and asked, "Will you govern with the same love for the people as Prefect Ma?"

sentences.zh: 徙知曹州，召為三司鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Caozhou, then summoned as Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Caozhou, then recalled to the capital as salt and iron commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 以默與富弼善，且論新法不便，出知濟、兗二州。

translations.literal: Because Mo was on good terms with Fu Bi and had argued that the New Policies were inconvenient, he was sent out to serve as prefect of Ji and Yan Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Because Mo was friendly with Fu Bi and had criticized the New Policies as impractical, he was sent out to serve as prefect of Ji and Yan Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 還，提舉三司帳司。

translations.literal: On his return, he was put in charge of the Accounts Office of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital, he was put in charge of the accounts office of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 為神宗言用兵形勢，及指畫河北山川道里，應對如流。

translations.literal: He explained to Emperor Shenzong the military situation and traced out the mountains, rivers, roads, and distances of Hebei. His replies flowed like water.
translations.idiomatic: He briefed Emperor Shenzong on the military situation and mapped out the mountains, rivers, roads, and distances of Hebei. His answers came as fluently as if from a prepared text.

sentences.zh: 神宗喜，將用之，大臣滋不悅，以提點京東刑獄。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong was pleased and was about to employ him, but the grand ministers grew increasingly displeased and had him made Judicial Commissioner for the Eastern Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and was about to give him greater office, but the chief ministers grew ever more displeased and had him appointed judicial commissioner for the Eastern Capital Circuit instead.

sentences.zh: 默性剛嚴疾惡，部吏有望風投檄去者。

translations.literal: Mo's nature was stern and strict, and he hated evil. Among the subordinate officials, some, catching wind of his reputation, submitted their resignations and left.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was stern by nature and hated corruption. Some subordinates, hearing of his reputation, resigned and fled.

sentences.zh: 金鄉令以賄著，其父方執政，詒書曰：「馬公素剛，汝有過，將不免。」

translations.literal: The magistrate of Jinxiang was notorious for bribes. His father was then in power and sent a letter saying, "Prefect Ma has always been stern. If you have faults, you will not escape punishment."
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Jinxiang was notorious for taking bribes. His father was then in high office and sent him a letter saying, "Prefect Ma has always been stern. If you have done wrong, you will not escape."

sentences.zh: 令懼，悉取不義之物焚撤之。

translations.literal: The magistrate, in fear, gathered all his ill-gotten goods, burned them, and cast them away.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate, terrified, gathered up all his ill-gotten goods, burned them, and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 改廣西轉運使，會安化等蠻歲饑內寇，默上平蠻方略，以為「勝負不在兵而在將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Transport Commissioner of Guangxi. At that time the Anhua and other tribes, suffering famine, raided inward. Mo submitted a strategy for pacifying the tribes, stating, "Victory and defeat lie not in troops but in generals.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner of Guangxi. At that time the Anhua and other tribes, suffering famine, raided the interior. Mo submitted a strategy for pacifying them, arguing that "victory and defeat depend not on troops but on generals.

sentences.zh: 富良宵遁，郭逵怯懦；

translations.literal: Fu Liang fled by night; Guo Kui was cowardly and weak;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang fled by night; Guo Kui was cowardly;

sentences.zh: 邕城陷沒，蘇緘老謬；

translations.literal: Yong city fell and was lost; Su Jian was old and mistaken;
translations.idiomatic: Yong city fell; Su Jian was old and misguided;

sentences.zh: 歸仁鋪覆軍，陳曙先走；

translations.literal: At Guiren Post the army was wiped out; Chen Shu fled first;
translations.idiomatic: At Guiren Post the army was annihilated and Chen Shu fled first;

sentences.zh: 昆侖關喪師，張守節不戰。

translations.literal: At Kunlun Pass the army was lost; Zhang Shoujie would not fight.
translations.idiomatic: At Kunlun Pass the army was lost because Zhang Shoujie refused to fight.

sentences.zh: 儂智高破亡，因狄青之智勇；

translations.literal: The destruction of Nong Zhigao came through Di Qing's wisdom and courage;
translations.idiomatic: Nong Zhigao was destroyed thanks to Di Qing's wisdom and courage;

sentences.zh: 歐希範之誅滅，乃杜杞之方略，此足驗矣。」

translations.literal: the extermination of Ou Xifan was due to Du Qi's strategy. This is sufficient proof."
translations.idiomatic: and Ou Xifan was exterminated through Du Qi's strategy. That is proof enough."

sentences.zh: 以疾求歸，知徐州。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested to return home and served as prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness, he asked to return home and was appointed prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬城利國監苦吳居厚之虐，默皆革之。

translations.literal: In a subordinate prefecture, the Liguo Superintendency suffered under Wu Juhou's cruelty. Mo reformed all of this.
translations.idiomatic: In a subordinate prefecture, the Liguo Superintendency had suffered under Wu Juhou's cruelty. Mo abolished every abusive practice.

sentences.zh: 召為司農少卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue for Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue for Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 司馬光為相，欲盡修祖宗法，問默以復鄉差衙前法如何，默曰：「不可。

translations.literal: When Sima Guang became chief minister, he wished to restore fully the laws of the ancestors and asked Mo what he thought of restoring the corvée system of district-assigned yaqian service. Mo said, "That cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang became chief minister, he wanted to restore the ancestral laws in full and asked Mo what he thought of reviving the district-assigned yaqian corvée system. Mo said, "That cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 如常平，自漢為良法，豈宜盡廢？

translations.literal: Take the Ever-Normal Granary system: since the Han it has been a good method—how can it be abolished entirely?
translations.idiomatic: Take the Ever-Normal Granary system: it has been a sound institution since Han times. How can it be abolished entirely?

sentences.zh: 去其害民者可也。」

translations.literal: Remove what harms the people—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Remove what harms the people, and that will suffice."

sentences.zh: 其後役人立為一州一縣法，常平提舉官省歸提刑司，頗自默發之。

translations.literal: Later, corvée laborers were organized under the one-prefecture-one-county law, and the supervisory posts for the Ever-Normal Granary were returned from the provincial level to the judicial commissioner's office—largely initiatives that issued from Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Later, corvée labor was reorganized under a one-prefecture-one-county system, and Ever-Normal Granary supervisors were transferred from the provincial level back to the judicial commissioner's office—reforms largely initiated by Mo.

sentences.zh: 除河東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Transport Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed transport commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 時議棄葭蘆、吳堡二砦，默奏控扼險阻，敵不可攻，棄之不便。

translations.literal: At the time the court debated abandoning the two forts of Jialu and Wubao. Mo memorialized that they controlled strategic passes and steep terrain and that the enemy could not attack them—abandoning them would be inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court debated abandoning the forts at Jialu and Wubao. Mo memorialized that they commanded strategic passes and rugged terrain and that the enemy could not easily attack them. Abandoning them would be a mistake.

sentences.zh: 由是二砦得不棄。

translations.literal: Because of this, the two forts were not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to this, the two forts were retained.

sentences.zh: 移兗州，請褒錄石介後，詔官其孫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yanzhou and requested that Shi Jie's descendants be honored and recorded. An edict granted office to his grandson.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Yanzhou and petitioned that Shi Jie's descendants be honored. An edict granted office to Shi Jie's grandson.

sentences.zh: 東州薦饑，流民大集，所振活數萬計。

translations.literal: The eastern prefectures suffered successive famines, and refugees gathered in great numbers. Those he relieved and kept alive numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern prefectures suffered repeated famines, and refugees gathered in great numbers. The people he saved numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 入拜衛尉卿，權工部侍郎，轉戶部。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Commandant of the Guards, then served as acting Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as commandant of the guards, served as acting vice minister of the Ministry of Works, and was then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 告老，以寶文閣待制復知徐州，改河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on grounds of age, then served again as prefect of Xuzhou with the title of Academician of the Baowen Pavilion, and was later changed to Chief Transport Commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on grounds of age, then returned as prefect of Xuzhou with the title of academician of the Baowen Pavilion, and was later appointed chief transport commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 初，元豐間，河決小吳，因不復塞，縱之北流。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Yuanfeng period, the Yellow River broke through at Xiaowu. Thereafter it was not dammed again and was allowed to flow north.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Yuanfeng era, the Yellow River broke through at Xiaowu. The breach was not repaired, and the river was allowed to flow north.

sentences.zh: 元祐議臣以為東流便，水官遂與之合。

translations.literal: During the Yuanyou period, the deliberating ministers held that an eastward flow would be convenient, and the water officials thereupon agreed with them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era, the deliberating ministers argued that an eastward course would be preferable, and the water officials agreed.

sentences.zh: 默與同時監司上議，以北流為便。

translations.literal: Mo, together with the supervisory commissioners of his time, submitted a memorial arguing that the northward flow was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Mo and the supervisory commissioners of his day submitted a memorial arguing that the northward course was preferable.

sentences.zh: 御史郭知章復請從東流，於是作東西馬頭，約水復故道，為長堤壅河之北流者，勞費甚大。

translations.literal: The censor Guo Zhizhang again requested following the eastward flow. Thereupon east-west horse-head dikes were built to constrain the water back to the old channel, and a long embankment was raised to block the river's northward flow. The labor and expense were very great.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Guo Zhizhang again petitioned for the eastward course. East-west horse-head dikes were then built to force the water back into its old channel, and a long embankment was raised to block the northward flow. The labor and expense were enormous.

sentences.zh: 明年，復決而北，竟不能使之東。

translations.literal: The next year the river broke through again and flowed north. In the end it could not be made to flow east.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the river broke through again and flowed north. In the end it could not be forced east.

sentences.zh: 久之，告老，提舉鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: After a long time he retired on grounds of age and was put in charge of Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he retired on grounds of age and was appointed supervisor of Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 紹聖時，坐附司馬光，落待制致仕。

translations.literal: During the Shaosheng period, he was punished for siding with Sima Guang, stripped of his dazhi title, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era he was punished for siding with Sima Guang, stripped of his academician title, and forced to retire.

sentences.zh: 元符三年，復之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfu, [the title] was restored to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfu his title was restored.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，以其子純請，贈開府儀同三司，加贈太保。

translations.literal: During the Shaoxing period, at the request of his son Chun, he was posthumously granted the rank of Kaifu Yitong Sansi, with an additional posthumous grant of Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing era, at the request of his son Chun, he was posthumously granted the rank of Kaifu Yitong Sansi, with an additional posthumous grant of Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 論曰：《詩》云：「時靡有爭，王心載寧。」

translations.literal: The discussion states: The Odes say, "When none contend, the king's heart is at peace."
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: The Odes say, "When none contend, the king's heart is at peace."

sentences.zh: 王安石之為相，可謂致天下之爭，而君心不寧矣。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi served as chief minister, it may be said that he brought contention to all under Heaven, and the ruler's heart was no longer at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi served as chief minister, he may be said to have brought contention to the realm, and the ruler's heart knew no peace.

sentences.zh: 孫覺、李常力諍新法，寧失故人之意，毅然去之而無悔，賢哉。

translations.literal: Sun Jue and Li Chang remonstrated forcefully against the New Policies. They would rather lose the regard of old friends, yet resolutely departed and had no regret—how worthy they were.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jue and Li Chang remonstrated forcefully against the New Policies. They were willing to forfeit the goodwill of old friends, yet left the cause resolutely and without regret. How worthy they were.

sentences.zh: 孔文仲之策制科，以微官慷慨論事，言雖不聽，而名徹上聰。

translations.literal: When Kong Wenzhong answered the decree examination, though a minor official he spoke boldly on public affairs. Though his words were not heeded, his name reached the emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Wenzhong took the decree examination, this minor official spoke boldly on affairs of state. Though the throne did not heed him, his name reached the emperor's ears.

sentences.zh: 安石既斥其人，又廢其科，何遷怒之甚耶！

translations.literal: Anshi had already driven the man out, yet he also abolished the examination itself—how excessive his displaced anger!
translations.idiomatic: Anshi had already driven the man out, yet he also abolished the examination itself—how excessive his displaced anger!

sentences.zh: 鮮于侁早識安石敗事，與呂誨同見幾先。

translations.literal: Xian Yushen early perceived that Anshi's policies would fail, and together with Lü Hui he saw the signs beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Xian Yushen early saw that Anshi's policies would fail, and together with Lü Hui he perceived what was coming before others did.

sentences.zh: 馬默用張方平薦為御史，至於盡言而不諱，方平止之而不聽，斯為不負知己矣。

translations.literal: Ma Mo, recommended by Zhang Fangping as censor, spoke his mind fully without reserve. Fangping tried to stop him but he would not listen—this was not failing the man who had known him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Mo entered the censorate on Zhang Fangping's recommendation and spoke his mind fully without reserve. Fangping tried to restrain him, but he would not listen—thus he did not betray the man who had known his worth.

sentences.zh: 李周之耿介，顧臨之用兵，李之純、王覿再黜而不改其正，亦足以見一時之多賢焉。

translations.literal: Li Zhou's integrity, Gu Lin's use of military affairs, Li Zhichun and Wang Di demoted repeatedly yet unchanged in their rectitude—these too suffice to show how many worthy men there were in that age.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhou's integrity, Gu Lin's expertise in military affairs, and Li Zhichun and Wang Di demoted again and again yet unbending in their principles—these too show how many worthy men that age could boast.
